﴿وَقالُوا﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿مَهْما﴾: a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿تَأْتِنا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter; نا is its object and its fāʿil (agent) is "you"; it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿بِهِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) تأتنا. ﴿مِنْ آيَةٍ﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِتَسْحَرَنا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); نا is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the agent is "you"; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تأتنا. ﴿بِها﴾: attached to تسحرنا. ﴿فَما﴾: ما is negative, functioning like laysa, and the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition مهما. ﴿نَحْنُ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of the nominative as its noun. ﴿بِمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: its khabar (predicate), and the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition.
﴿لَكَ﴾: attached to the khabar مؤمنين; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the two conditional clauses together are the khabar of مهما.

daas-irab:133-133.t:
﴿فَأَرْسَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. ﴿الطُّوفانَ﴾: its object. ﴿وَالْجَرادَ وَالْقُمَّلَ وَالضَّفادِعَ وَالدَّمَ﴾: conjoined nouns. ﴿آياتٍ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative with the kasra, being a sound feminine plural. ﴿مُفَصَّلاتٍ﴾: adjective (ṣifa).
﴿فَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾: a past verb and agent, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَكانُوا قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:11-11.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْناكُمْ﴾: the lām falls in the answer to the oath; [خلقناكم is] a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object. ﴿ثُمَّ صَوَّرْناكُمْ﴾: conjoined. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿قُلْنا لِلْمَلائِكَةِ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and نا is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined.
﴿اسْجُدُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لِآدَمَ﴾: a noun, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, a diptote because it is a proper name and non-Arabic; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اسجدوا; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَسَجَدُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception. ﴿إِبْلِيسَ﴾: the excepted, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿لَمْ﴾: jussive-governing. ﴿يَكُنْ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm); its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he" (هو). ﴿مِنَ السَّاجِدِينَ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of يكن; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive.

daas-irab:12-12.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما مَنَعَكَ﴾: ما is an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject); منعك is a past verb and its object, its fāʿil (agent) being "you" (أنت) [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʿil of منعك is a latent third-person pronoun referring to ما, and the kāf ("you") is its object]; the clause is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate). ﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle. ﴿لا﴾: redundant (zāʾida).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the verb ﴿تَسْجُدَ﴾ and the maṣdar-forming particle before it is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by a preposition, i.e. "what prevented you from prostrating"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before them. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb for past time, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of accusative (manṣūb), attached to تسجد. ﴿أَمَرْتُكَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb. ﴿أَنَا﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ﴾: khabar, to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached, because it is an elative noun (ism al-tafḍīl) whose original form is أخير. ﴿خَلَقْتَنِي﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, the nūn being for protection (wiqāya); the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.
﴿مِنْ نارٍ﴾: attached to the verb before them, and the clause ﴿وَخَلَقْتَهُ﴾ is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ طِينٍ﴾: attached to the verb before them.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَاهْبِطْ مِنْها﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت), and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَما﴾: ما is negating and the fāʾ is conjunctive. ﴿يَكُونُ﴾: a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb in the sense of "it is permissible", to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached. ﴿أَنْ تَتَكَبَّرَ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to the verb before them; the clause فما يكون is conjoined. ﴿فَاخْرُجْ﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾: inna, and the kāf is its noun. ﴿مِنَ الصَّاغِرِينَ﴾: a noun, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:14-15.t: ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْظِرْنِي إِلى يَوْمِ﴾: an imperative verb used for supplication, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُبْعَثُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause أنظرني is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ﴾: like إنك من الصاغرين.

daas-irab:16-16.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: its parsing has gone before. ﴿فَبِما﴾: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); the bāʾ is a preposition; ما is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun particle). ﴿أَغْوَيْتَنِي﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the verb and what precedes it is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted verb of oath; the oath clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿لَأَقْعُدَنَّ﴾: the lām falls in the answer to the oath; أقعدن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and its fāʿil is "I" (أنا). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: attached to أقعدن. ﴿صِراطَكَ﴾: accusative by removal of the preposition, or an adverb of place attached to the verb before it. ﴿الْمُسْتَقِيمَ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). The clause لأقعدن has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.

daas-irab:17-17.t:
﴿ثُمَّ﴾: conjunctive. ﴿لَآتِيَنَّهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil (agent) is "I" (أنا), the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the lām falls in the answer to the oath. The clause has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath. ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before them. ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the hāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وَعَنْ أَيْمانِهِمْ وَعَنْ شَمائِلِهِمْ﴾: conjoined. ﴿وَلا تَجِدُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil is "you" (أنت); لا is negating. ﴿أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾: first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿شاكِرِينَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, or a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿اخْرُجْ﴾ منها: an imperative verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); its fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿مَذْؤُماً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مَدْحُوراً﴾: a second ḥāl. ﴿لَمَنْ﴾: the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تَبِعَكَ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ are attached; its fāʿil is "he" (هو), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَأَمْلَأَنَّ﴾: the lām falls in the answer to the oath. ﴿أملأن﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is "I" (أنا). ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾: its object. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: attached to the verb before them. ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
The clause has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath, and the answer to the oath has taken the place of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَيا آدَمُ﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and [آدم is] a singular proper-name one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of accusative (manṣūb); the wāw is conjunctive. ﴿اسْكُنْ﴾: an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you" (أنت); the clause is conjoined to the clause اخرج. ﴿أَنْتَ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun in the verb. ﴿وَزَوْجُكَ﴾: a noun conjoined to أنت. ﴿الْجَنَّةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَكُلا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined by the fāʾ. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a preposition. ﴿حَيْثُ﴾: an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive (majrūr) by min; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before them. ﴿شِئْتُما﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn; the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and mā is for the dual; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the alif is the fāʿil. ﴿هذِهِ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الشَّجَرَةَ﴾: badal (substitute), accusative with the fatḥa. ﴿فَتَكُونا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the alif of the dual is its noun. The implied an and the verb after it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to what precedes it, the implied form being: "let there be from you no approaching, and so wrongdoing". ﴿مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: attached to an omitted khabar (predicate).

daas-irab:20-20.t:
﴿فَوَسْوَسَ لَهُمَا الشَّيْطانُ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and الشيطان is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined.
﴿لِيُبْدِيَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وسوس. ﴿لَهُمَا﴾: attached to يبدي. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿وُورِيَ عَنْهُما﴾: a passive past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "it" (هو). ﴿مِنْ سَوْآتِهِما﴾: attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَقالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما نَهاكُما﴾: ما is negating, and [نهاكما is] a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the kāf is its object; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿رَبُّكُما﴾: fāʿil.
﴿عَنْ﴾: a preposition. ﴿هذِهِ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of genitive by the preposition. ﴿الشَّجَرَةِ﴾: badal (substitute), genitive. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ تَكُونا مَلَكَيْنِ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; the alif of the dual is its noun and ملكين its khabar (predicate); the interpreted maṣdar from the accusative-governing an and the verb is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), i.e. "for dislike of your being two angels". ﴿أَوْ تَكُونا مِنَ الْخالِدِينَ﴾: conjoined.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وَقاسَمَهُما﴾: a past verb; the hāʾ is its object, the mīm and the alif are for the dual, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (هو), referring to Satan. ﴿إِنِّي﴾: inna, and the yāʾ of the speaker is its noun. ﴿لَكُما﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to الناصحين after it. ﴿لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿من النَّاصِحِينَ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of inna. The nominal clause ﴿إِنِّي لَكُما لَمِنَ النَّاصِحِينَ﴾ has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath, and the clause ﴿قاسَمَهُما﴾ is conjoined to the clause قال ما نهاكما.

daas-irab:22-22.t:
﴿فَدَلَّاهُما بِغُرُورٍ﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and [دلاهما is] a past verb to which the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); the fāʿil (agent) is "he" (هو) and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾: [لما is] a temporal adverb ("when"), and the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿ذاقَا الشَّجَرَةَ﴾: a past verb; the alif of the dual is its fāʿil and الشجرة its object; the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَدَتْ لَهُما سَوْآتُهُما﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, which was dropped to avoid the meeting of two sukūns; the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it, and سوآتهما is the fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَطَفِقا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the alif is its noun.
﴿يَخْصِفانِ عَلَيْهِما﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the alif is its fāʿil, and a preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb, as is likewise the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنْ وَرَقِ﴾. ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَناداهُما رَبُّهُما﴾: a past verb, its object and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَلَمْ أَنْهَكُما﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter because it ends in a weak letter; the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تِلْكُمَا﴾: تِ is a demonstrative, indeclinable on kasra, in the position of genitive by عن; the lām is for distance, the kāf for address, and mā for the dual. ﴿الشَّجَرَةَ﴾: badal (substitute). ﴿وَأَقُلْ لَكُما﴾: an imperfect verb conjoined to أنهكما, jussive like it, with sukūn; the following preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِنَّ الشَّيْطانَ لَكُما عَدُوٌّ﴾: inna, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to عدو, and ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾
is an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:23-23.t:
﴿قالا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: a one addressed (munādā) in construct, accusative (manṣūb). ﴿ظَلَمْنا أَنْفُسَنا﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: conditional, and the wāw is conjunctive. ﴿لَمْ﴾: jussive-governing. ﴿تَغْفِرْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm); it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).
﴿وَتَرْحَمْنا﴾: conjoined. ﴿لَنَكُونَنَّ﴾: the lām falls in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); نكونن is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we" (نحن). ﴿مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to its omitted khabar (predicate); the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a condition not joined with the fāʾ … and the apodosis has made the answer to the oath unnecessary. It is also permissible to parse the clause لنكونن as the answer to the oath, the lām being the lām of the oath, and it has made the apodosis unnecessary.

daas-irab:134-134.t:
﴿وَلَمَّا﴾: a conditional adverb, and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّجْزُ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and الرجز is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation). The clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the response to لما. ﴿يا مُوسَى﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative. ﴿ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿لَنا﴾ are attached; the agent is "you"; ﴿رَبَّكَ﴾ is its object, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِما﴾: maṣdarī, interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb ادع. Or ما is relative. ﴿عَهِدَ﴾: the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عِنْدَكَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to the verb عهد. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾: the lām is the one that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); إن is a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كَشَفْتَ﴾: a past verb and agent. ﴿الرِّجْزُ﴾ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; as the object it is الرِّجْزَ]: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عَنَّا﴾: attached to كشف. ﴿الرِّجْزُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: the source repeats this item]. ﴿لَنُؤْمِنَنَّ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥ because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its agent is "we" (نحن), and the lām occurs in the response to the oath. ﴿لَكَ﴾: attached to the verb before them, and the clause occurs as the response to the oath. The clause كشف is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿لَنُرْسِلَنَّ﴾ is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مَعَكَ﴾: an adverb, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَنِي﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural; the nūn was dropped for annexation. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa.

daas-irab:135-135.t:
﴿فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمُ الرِّجْزَ﴾: see the i'rab of the previous verse. ﴿إِلى أَجَلٍ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الرجز.
﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بالِغُوهُ﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation), and the nūn was dropped for annexation; the clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of أجل. ﴿إِذا﴾: of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَنْكُثُونَ﴾: the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:136-136.t:
﴿فَانْتَقَمْنا مِنْهُمْ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and نا is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined, and likewise the clause ﴿فَأَغْرَقْناهُمْ فِي الْيَمِّ﴾ "so We drowned them in the sea". ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾: anna, and the hāʾ is its noun. ﴿كَذَّبُوا﴾:
a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿بِآياتِنا﴾ are attached; the wāw is its agent, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of anna. The interpreted maṣdar formed from anna, its noun and its khabar is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ: "We drowned them because of their denial ...". ﴿وَكانُوا﴾: kāna, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿عَنْها﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar ﴿غافِلِينَ﴾, and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:137-137.t:
﴿وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first object. The clause is conjoined. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). The clause is in the position of the accusative as khabar (predicate), and the clause كانوا يستضعفون is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مَشارِقَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْأَرْضِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمَغارِبَهَا﴾: conjoined to مشارق. ﴿الَّتِي﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as an adjective. ﴿بارَكْنا﴾: a past verb, and نا is its agent. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) باركنا, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ﴾: a past verb and its agent; the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾: an adjective of كلمة, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif because of impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿عَلى﴾: a preposition. ﴿بَنِي﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural, and the nūn was dropped for annexation. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the fatḥa, a diptote because it is a proper noun and non-Arab. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is maṣdarī, interpreted together with the verb after it, ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb تمت.
﴿وَدَمَّرْنا﴾: a past verb and agent. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined.
﴿كانَ﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ﴾: an imperfect verb and agent. ﴿وَقَوْمُهُ﴾: conjoined to فرعون. The clause is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of kāna.. and the clause of kāna with its noun and its khabar is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما كانُوا يَعْرِشُونَ﴾: conjoined.

daas-irab:138-138.t:
﴿وَجاوَزْنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِبَنِي﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿إِسْرائِيلَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْبَحْرَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source; البحر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جاوزنا].
﴿فَأَتَوْا عَلى قَوْمٍ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its agent, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَعْكُفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and agent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of قوم. ﴿عَلى أَصْنامٍ﴾: attached to the verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: attached to an omitted adjective of أصنام. ﴿قالُوا﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا مُوسَى﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿اجْعَلْ لَنا﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the agent is "you". ﴿إِلهاً﴾: its object. ﴿كَما﴾: the kāf is a preposition, and ما is maṣdarī or relative. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿آلِهَةٌ﴾. The interpreted maṣdar formed from ما and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of إلها, i.e., "a worshipped god like their gods ....". ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّكُمْ قَوْمٌ﴾: inna and its noun [and khabar]; the clause إنكم قوم .. is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl), a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿تَجْهَلُونَ﴾: the clause is an adjective of قوم.

daas-irab:139-139.t:
﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasr, in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿مُتَبَّرٌ﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of متبر. ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِيهِ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. The nominal clause إنّ هؤلاء .. is resumptive. ﴿وَباطِلٌ﴾: a fronted khabar. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun, and the clause يعملون is in the position of the accusative as its khabar. The clause كانوا is the ṣila, with no grammatical position, and the nominal clause وباطل ما كانوا يعملون .. is conjoined.

daas-irab:140-140.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَغَيْرَ﴾: a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hamza is interrogative. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. ﴿أَبْغِيكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ because of heaviness (thiqal). The kāf is genitive by removal of the preposition: "I seek for you". ﴿إِلهاً﴾: tamyīz (specification). The clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَهُوَ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
The wāw is circumstantial. ﴿فَضَّلَكُمْ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ﴾ are attached, and the fāʿil (agent) is "he". The kāf is its object, and the verbal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. The nominal clause وهو فضلكم is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:141-141.t:
In Sūrat al-Baqara, verse 49, it is نجيناكم instead of أنجيناكم .. and ويذبحون أبناءكم instead of يقتلون أبناءكم.
﴿وَإِذْ﴾: mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember the time ....", and the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation).
﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, fāʿil (agent) and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿سُوءَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause is circumstantial; the clause ﴿يُقَتِّلُونَ أَبْناءَكُمْ﴾ is a badal (substitute) of the clause ﴿يَسُومُونَكُمْ﴾. ﴿وَفِي ذلِكُمْ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿بَلاءٌ﴾. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾: attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of بلاء. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾: adjective, and the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:142-142.t:
﴿وَواعَدْنا مُوسى﴾: a past verb, fāʿil (agent) and first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ثَلاثِينَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَيْلَةً﴾: tamyīz (specification). The clause is resumptive. ﴿وَأَتْمَمْناها﴾: a past verb; نا is its agent and ها its object. ﴿بِعَشْرٍ﴾: attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَتَمَّ مِيقاتُ رَبِّهِ﴾: a past verb and its agent. ﴿أَرْبَعِينَ﴾: its object [Translator's note: so in the source; تمّ is intransitive, and أربعين is commonly parsed as ḥāl], and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَيْلَةً﴾: tamyīz.
﴿قالَ مُوسى﴾: a past verb and agent. ﴿لِأَخِيهِ﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns.
The hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation). ﴿هارُونَ﴾: badal (substitute), genitive with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, a diptote because it is a proper noun and non-Arab; the clause is conjoined. ﴿اخْلُفْنِي﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is implied as "you". ﴿فِي قَوْمِي﴾: attached to the verb before them. ﴿وَأَصْلِحْ﴾: conjoined to اخلف. ﴿وَلا تَتَّبِعْ﴾: the prohibitive lā and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the agent is "you". ﴿سَبِيلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:143-143.t:
﴿وَلَمَّا﴾: a conditional adverb, and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿جاءَ مُوسى لِمِيقاتِنا﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and موسى is its fāʿil (agent). The clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (annexation). ﴿وَكَلَّمَهُ رَبُّهُ﴾: a past verb; the hāʾ is its object and ربّه its agent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive conditional. ﴿رَبِّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative with the fatḥa implied on the letter before the first-person yāʾ. ﴿أَرِنِي﴾: a verb of supplication, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter because it is weak-final; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya). The yāʾ is its first object, and its second object is omitted, its implied form being "Yourself"; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". ﴿أَنْظُرْ إِلَيْكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the response to the request; its agent is latent, and [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them; the response to the request together with its verb is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَنْ﴾: a particle governing the accusative. ﴿تَرانِي﴾: an accusative imperfect verb, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif, its appearance prevented by impossibility (taʿadhdhur); the nūn is for protection and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the speech reported. ﴿وَلكِنِ﴾: a particle of rectification (istidrāk), and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿انْظُرْ إِلَى الْجَبَلِ﴾: an imperative verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; its agent is "you", and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَإِنِ﴾: إن is a jussive conditional, and the fāʾ is a conjunction. ﴿اسْتَقَرَّ﴾: a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿مَكانَهُ﴾: an adverb of place attached to استقر.
﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾: a particle of the future, and the fāʾ links the apodosis. ﴿تَرانِي﴾: a nominative imperfect verb, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿فَلَمَّا تَجَلَّى رَبُّهُ لِلْجَبَلِ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; لما is conditional; تجلى is a past verb with its agent, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿جَعَلَهُ دَكًّا﴾: a past verb and its two objects; the agent is "he", and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. ﴿وَخَرَّ مُوسى﴾: a past verb and agent. ﴿صَعِقاً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَلَمَّا أَفاقَ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; لما is a jussive conditional [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere لما is described as a non-jussive conditional adverb], and [أفاق is] a past verb whose agent is latent. ﴿قالَ﴾: the clause has no grammatical position, being the response to لما. ﴿سُبْحانَكَ﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the kāf is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa. ﴿تُبْتُ﴾: a past verb and its agent. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: attached to تبت. The clause is the speech reported. ﴿وَأَنَا أَوَّلُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the clause is conjoined. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:24-24.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿اهْبِطُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar (predicate) ﴿عَدُوٌّ﴾; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾: attached to an omitted khabar, and likewise the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾. ﴿مُسْتَقَرٌّ﴾: mubtadaʾ placed after. ﴿وَمَتاعٌ﴾: conjoined. ﴿إِلى حِينٍ﴾: attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of متاع, i.e. "provision extending until a time"; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:25-25.t:
﴿قالَ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿فِيها تَحْيَوْنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, to which the preposition and its genitive noun before it are attached (mutaʿalliq); the wāw is its fāʿil (agent).
The clause is conjoined. ﴿وَفِيها تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْها تُخْرَجُونَ﴾: conjoined.

daas-irab:26-26.t:
﴿يا بَنِي﴾: يا is a vocative particle; بني is a one addressed (munādā) in construct, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural, and the nūn has been dropped for the iḍāfa. ﴿آدَمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, a non-Arabic proper name. ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكُمْ لِباساً﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); نا is its fāʿil (agent) and لباسا its object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُوارِي﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness; the fāʿil is "it" (هو). ﴿سَوْآتِكُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of لباس. ﴿وَرِيشاً﴾: conjoined. ﴿وَلِباسُ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لباس is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿التَّقْوى﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the kasra implied on the alif. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: its khabar (predicate). The nominal clause ذلك خير is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ لباس. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿مِنْ آياتِ﴾: attached to its omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾: لعل, and the hāʾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ is in the position of nominative as its khabar.
The clause ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t:
﴿يا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾: its parsing was given in the previous verse. ﴿لا يَفْتِنَنَّكُمُ﴾: يفتننّ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the kāf is its object and the mīm is for the masculine plural; ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَما﴾: the kāf is a preposition; ما is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun particle). ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿أَبَوَيْكُمْ﴾: its object, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ; the nūn has been dropped for the iḍāfa, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb أخرج. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the maṣdariyya ما and the verb after it is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being: "let not Satan tempt you with a temptation like the temptation [of your parents]". ﴿يَنْزِعُ عَنْهُما لِباسَهُما﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and لباسهما is its object; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِيُرِيَهُما﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the fāʿil is "he" (هو) and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; and it is in the accusative by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation. ﴿سَوْآتِهِما﴾: its second object, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. The interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdariyya an and the verb after it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb ينزع. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna, and the hāʾ is its noun, and the clause ﴿يَراكُمْ﴾ is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of inna; the clause ﴿إِنَّهُ يَراكُمْ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿هُوَ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun in the verb يراكم. ﴿وَقَبِيلُهُ﴾: a noun conjoined to the nominative pronoun in يراكم. ﴿حَيْثُ﴾: an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of genitive by a preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb يراكم. ﴿لا تَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is its object; لا is negating; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿جَعَلْنَا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its two objects; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna. The clause ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا﴾ is causal, with no grammatical position.
﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾: attached to the verb جعلنا, and the clause ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾: a conditional adverb, non-jussive; the wāw is resumptive. ﴿فَعَلُوا فاحِشَةً﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿وَجَدْنا عَلَيْها آباءَنا﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); نا is its fāʿil and آباءنا its object; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl), a mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿أَمَرَنا بِها﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause ﴿اللَّهُ أَمَرَنا بِها﴾ is conjoined. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause ﴿لا يَأْمُرُ بِالْفَحْشاءِ﴾ is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as its khabar; the nominal clause ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَأْمُرُ﴾ is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَتَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hamza is for interrogation; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: attached to the verb before it. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ﴿لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:29-29.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَمَرَ﴾: a past verb. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker; the yāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to أمر. ﴿وَأَقِيمُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, with its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to أقيموا. ﴿كُلِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مَسْجِدٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَادْعُوهُ﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined. ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ. ﴿لَهُ﴾: attached to the active participle مخلصين before it.
﴿الدِّينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi of the active participle, whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun. ﴿كَما﴾: the kāf is a preposition; ما is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun particle). ﴿بَدَأَكُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil being "He" (هو), and the kāf is its object; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from the maṣdar-forming particle and the verb is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being: "you will return, a returning like His beginning of you".
The clause ﴿تَعُودُونَ﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿فَرِيقاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed before the verb ﴿هَدى﴾. The clause ﴿فَرِيقاً هَدى﴾ is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "guiding a party and leading astray a party". ﴿وَفَرِيقاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "and He led astray" (وأضل); the clause is conjoined, and the clause ﴿حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الضَّلالَةُ﴾ is in the position of accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of فريق. ﴿إِنَّهُمُ﴾: inna, and the hāʾ is its noun. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا الشَّياطِينَ أَوْلِياءَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its two objects. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted adjective of أولياء; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the clause ﴿إِنَّهُمُ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾: anna, its noun and its khabar, which have taken the place of the two objects of يحسبون.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿يا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾: given in verse 25. [Translator's note: so in the source; the parsing was given in verse 26.] ﴿خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil (agent) and ﴿زِينَتَكُمْ﴾ its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before it. ﴿كُلِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مَسْجِدٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا﴾: conjoined to خذوا. ﴿وَلا تُسْرِفُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn because it is preceded by the prohibitive lā; the two clauses كلوا and لا تسرفوا are conjoined. The clause ﴿إِنَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿لا يُحِبُّ﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna.

daas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause ﴿حَرَّمَ زِينَةَ اللَّهِ﴾ is its khabar (predicate). ﴿الَّتِي﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective (ṣifa) of زينة, and the clause ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالطَّيِّباتِ﴾: conjoined to زينة, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa, [being] a sound feminine plural. ﴿مِنَ الرِّزْقِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿قُلْ﴾: its parsing has gone before. ﴿هِيَ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾: attached to the khabar, and the clause ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي الْحَياةِ﴾: attached to the verb. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: an adjective of الحياة, genitive (majrūr) with the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif because it is impossible to pronounce. ﴿خالِصَةً﴾: a ḥāl, accusative. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to خالصة. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun): "We detail the signs, a detailing like that". The clause ﴿نُفَصِّلُ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position, and the clause ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is an adjective.

daas-irab:33-33.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾: the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: [inna] restrained [by mā] and the restraining [mā] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿حَرَّمَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). [Translator's note: so in the source, which then makes ربي the fāʿil.] ﴿رَبِّيَ﴾: the fāʿil of حرم, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker; the yāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْفَواحِشَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ما ظَهَرَ مِنْها﴾: ما is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a badal (substitute) from الفواحش, and the clause ظهر is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما بَطَنَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿وَالْإِثْمَ وَالْبَغْيَ﴾: conjoined to الفواحش. ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to البغي. ﴿الْحَقِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿إِنَّما حَرَّمَ﴾ is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَأَنْ تُشْرِكُوا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is likewise conjoined: "my Lord has forbidden indecencies and polytheism".
﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: attached to تشركوا. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطاناً﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm), to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and سلطانا is its object; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾: the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined, the implied form being: "He has forbidden polytheism and saying what you do not know". ﴿عَلَى﴾: a preposition. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the name of Majesty, in the position of genitive (majrūr); [the preposition and its genitive noun] are attached to the verb before them. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the clause ﴿لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is its ṣila.

daas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ﴾: attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first. ﴿أُمَّةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَجَلٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿إذا﴾: a conditional adverb, non-jussive, and the clause ﴿جاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿ساعَةً﴾: an adverb of time; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. The clause ﴿وَلا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾ is conjoined.

daas-irab:35-35.t: ﴿يا بَنِي آدَمَ﴾: its parsing has gone before. ﴿إِمَّا﴾: إن is a jussive conditional particle, and ما is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of jussive (majzūm); the kāf is its object. ﴿رُسُلٌ﴾: its fāʿil (agent); the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿رُسُلٌ﴾; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the wāw is its fāʿil, and آياتي its object, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra; the yāʾ is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as an adjective of رسل. ﴿فَمَنِ﴾: من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the fāʾ in فمن connects the answer to the preceding إمّا, the whole of فمن اتقى… being that apodosis]. ﴿اتَّقى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and it is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); likewise ﴿أَصْلَحَ﴾. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ connects the apodosis, and لا is negating, without governing effect. ﴿خَوْفٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the clause ﴿فَمَنِ اتَّقى﴾ is resumptive. ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the clause ﴿يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ is in the position of nominative as its khabar; the clause ﴿وَلا هُمْ﴾ is conjoined.

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq); the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause ﴿اسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها﴾ is conjoined. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾: its khabar (predicate); the clause ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الذين. ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾: attached to the khabar placed after, ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾; the nominal clause is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ is conjoined.

dervis-irab:35-37.t:
* I'rab:
(يا بَنِي آدَمَ) Its i'rab has been given many times before. (إِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ) The speech is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), introduced to set out the matter of sending messengers. إنْ is conditional, assimilated into the redundant (zāʾida) «ما» which reinforces the conditional meaning; for that reason its verb must take the heavy or the light nūn of emphasis. يأتينكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; رسل is the fāʿil (agent); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رسل. Making the messengers from among them cuts off the argument more decisively and leaves less room for excuse. (يَقُصُّونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِي) The clause is also an adjective of رسل; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقصون; آياتي is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَمَنِ اتَّقى وَأَصْلَحَ فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) This conditional sentence is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the preceding condition; the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa); مَن is a conditional noun and mubtadaʾ (subject); the fāʾ in His words فلا خوف is connective; the i'rab of what follows has been given many times before. (وَالَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is a relative noun and mubtadaʾ; the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is the ṣila (relative clause); استكبروا عنها is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of الذين, the linking element being the demonstrative, as mentioned before; هم is a mubtadaʾ, and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar «خالدون»; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a second khabar of الذين. (فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآياتِهِ) The fāʾ is resumptive; مَن is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, i.e. no one is more unjust; أظلم is the khabar of «من»; ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أظلم; the clause افترى has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افترى; كذبا is a mafʿūl bihi, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause كذب بآياته is conjoined to the clause افترى. (أُولئِكَ يَنالُهُمْ نَصِيبُهُمْ مِنَ الْكِتابِ) The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; the clause ينالهم is the khabar; نصيبهم is the fāʿil of ينالهم; من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (حَتَّى إِذا جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا يَتَوَفَّوْنَهُمْ) حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition, or an inceptive particle (ibtidāʾiyya); discussion of this expression has been given before, so refresh your memory of it. إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; the clause جاءتهم رسلنا is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يتوفونهم is a ḥāl of رسلنا, i.e. taking them in death. (قالُوا أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) The clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivizing condition; أين is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ; the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); the clause كنتم is the ṣila of the relative; the tāʾ is the noun (ism) of kāna and the clause تدعون its khabar; من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or attached to تدعون. (قالُوا ضَلُّوا عَنَّا وَشَهِدُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَنَّهُمْ كانُوا كافِرِينَ) The clause is the answer to an implied question, as though it had been said: What did your objects of worship do, and those whom you used to call upon? So they answered that they had strayed away. The clause ضلوا is maqūl al-qawl; the clause شهدوا is conjoined to the clause قالوا, or is resumptive; على أنفسهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شهدوا; أنّ and what falls within its scope are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to شهدوا; the clause كانوا كافرين is the khabar of «أنّ».

dervis-irab:38-41.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ادَّارَكُوا): i.e. تداركوا, meaning they followed one another into the Fire. Its origin is تداركوا: the tāʾ was turned into a dāl, made quiescent and assimilated into the dāl, and then the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in. How this happens will be explained in the Benefits section.
(أخراهم وأولاهم): It is possible that [أخرى] is «فُعلى», the feminine of the «أفعل» that denotes comparison (mufāḍala); on this view the meaning is: the last of them in rank — the followers and the lowly — [said] to the first of them in rank — the leaders, the masters and the chiefs. It is also possible that «أخرى» means "last" (آخِرة), the feminine of «آخِر» as opposed to «أوّل», not the feminine of the «آخَر» of comparison; from this usage is His words, the Exalted: «ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى». Perhaps this is the more apparent [meaning] in the verse.
(الضِّعْفِ): Abū ʿUbayda said: الضعف is the like of a thing once. Al-Azharī said: It is as people use it in the course of their speech. In the speech of the Arabs الضعف is the like and more, and it is not restricted to two likes; rather you say: «هذا ضعفه», meaning twice it and three times it, because الضعف originally means an unlimited increase. Do you not see His words, the Exalted: «فأولئك لهم جزاء الضعف»? He did not mean by it one like nor two likes; the most fitting thing is to make it ten times, as in His words, the Exalted: «من جاء بالحسنة فله عشر أمثالها». So the minimum of الضعف is limited, namely one like, and its maximum is unlimited. In al-Qāmūs: «ضِعف of a thing, with kasra, is its like, and its two ضعف are its two likes; الضعف is the like and more. One says: لك ضعفه, meaning twice it and three times it, because it is an unlimited increase».
(يَلِجَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: «ولج الشيء في غيره يلج, of the pattern of وعد, ولوجا [= the thing entered into another]; and أولجته إيلاجا: I made it enter».
(سَمِّ): السم is said with all three vowels on the sīn. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «السم is what kills, mostly with fatḥa; its plural is سموم and سمام, like فلس and فلوس, and also سِمام, like سهم and سهام. The ḍamma is the dialect of the people of al-ʿĀliya, and the kasra the dialect of Banū Tamīm ... And السم is the eye of the needle; it has the three dialectal forms, and its plural is سمام». That is what is meant in the verse, but the Seven [readers] read it with fatḥa, and it has been read anomalously (shādhdhan) with kasra and ḍamma. The eye of the needle is proverbial for the narrowness of a passage; one says: «أضيق من خرت الإبرة» (narrower than the eye of a needle). They called the skilled guide خِرّيت, because he finds his way through narrow places likened to the eyes of needles. And the camel is proverbial for great bulk. Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
لا بأس في القوم من طول ومن عظم ... جسم البغال وأحلام العصافير
(There is no harm in the people as regards height and bulk: the bodies of mules and the minds of sparrows.) That is: no harm or hurt befalls these people from the side of height and thickness.
In it there is mockery of them: their bodies are like the bodies of mules, and their minds like the minds of sparrows — if sparrows have minds; he means that they have no minds.
(غَواشٍ): the plural of غاشية, which is a covering.

* I'rab:
(قالَ ادْخُلُوا فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ فِي النَّارِ) The speech is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), relating what Allah will say to them on the Day of Resurrection. قال is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هو"; the clause ادخلوا is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); في أمم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being among the number of nations, in their throng, accompanying them; it has also been said that they are attached to ادخلوا, the meaning being "among the number of nations". The clause قد خلت is a naʿt (adjective) of أمم; من قبلكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second adjective; من الجن والإنس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted third adjective; في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) of His words:
«في أمم». The adverbial expressions (ẓurūf) are figurative, and they will be discussed. Abū Ḥayyān said:
في النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خلت», on the sense that their entry into it came before; or to an omitted adjective of الأمم, i.e. among nations preceding in time, being of the jinn and mankind, being in the Fire. Abū Ḥayyān went on at length in what has no use. (كُلَّما دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَها) كلما is an adverb of time containing the meaning of condition; the clause دخلت أمة is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, or has no grammatical position if we take «ما» as a particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī); the clause لعنت أختها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussivizing condition, and the adverbial sentence is part of the completion of maqūl al-qawl. (حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا فِيها جَمِيعاً) حتى is a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition, or an inceptive particle; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis, i.e. to قالت that follows; the clause اداركوا is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اداركوا; جميعا is a ḥāl. (قالَتْ أُخْراهُمْ لِأُولاهُمْ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا. In لأولاهم the lām is a preposition of cause, i.e. for their sake, or of communication (tablīgh); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قالت. (رَبَّنا هؤُلاءِ أَضَلُّونا فَآتِهِمْ عَذاباً ضِعْفاً مِنَ النَّارِ) ربنا is a muḍāf vocative (munādā) from which the vocative particle has been omitted; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause أضلونا its khabar (predicate); the sentence ربنا هؤلاء is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl. فآتهم: the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; آتهم is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عذابا is a second mafʿūl bihi; ضعفا is an adjective of «عذابا»; من النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second adjective. (قالَ: لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ وَلكِنْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ)
The sentence of saying is resumptive; لكل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ضعف is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying of the Exalted. In ولكن the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); لا is negating; تعلمون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn. (وَقالَتْ أُولاهُمْ لِأُخْراهُمْ فَما كانَ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنا مِنْ فَضْلٍ) Conjoined to what preceded. The fāʾ is a conjunction: it conjoins the speech after it to the words of Allah the Exalted to the lowly ones, "for each is a double", i.e. it has been established that you have no superiority over us. ما is negating; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of defective كان; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; فضل is genitive in form and the ism of kāna in position; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun. That is: we and you are equal in going astray and in deserving the punishment. (فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, i.e. if it has become clear to you and you know it, and then you persisted in your contrary position, then taste; العذاب is its object; in بما the bāʾ is a causal preposition and ما is maṣdariyya, i.e. because of your earning; the clause تكسبون is the khabar of كنتم. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا عَنْها لا تُفَتَّحُ لَهُمْ أَبْوابُ السَّماءِ) Resumptive speech introduced to confirm the fate of the disbelievers. إنّ and its noun; the clause كذبوا بآياتنا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, having no grammatical position; the clause استكبروا is conjoined to the clause كفروا [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is كذبوا]; عنها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استكبروا; the clause لا تفتح is the khabar of إنّ; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تفتح; أبواب السماء is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَلا يَدْخُلُونَ الْجَنَّةَ حَتَّى يَلِجَ الْجَمَلُ فِي سَمِّ الْخِياطِ) This clause is conjoined to the clause لا تفتح لهم; حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; في سم الخياط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يلج. (وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُجْرِمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a recompense like that; المجرمين is a mafʿūl bihi. (لَهُمْ مِنْ جَهَنَّمَ مِهادٌ) The nominal sentence may be circumstantial or resumptive; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مهاد is a delayed mubtadaʾ; من جهنم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of جهنم [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. an adjective of مهاد fronted before it]. (وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ غَواشٍ وَكَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ) Conjoined; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; غواش is a delayed mubtadaʾ, the ḍamma being implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. More will be said about it in the Benefits section.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, the Exalted: «حتى يلج الجمل سم الخياط» there is a rhetorical figure called al-madhhab al-kalāmī (the dialectical method). Ibn al-Muʿtazz says in his book al-Badīʿ that al-Jāḥiẓ gave it this name. They define it as the speaker's arguing for what he wishes to establish with a proof that blunts the weapon of the stubborn opponent and cuts off his evidence, in the manner of the scholars of kalām.
For the science of kalām consists in establishing the principles of religion by rational proofs and decisive demonstrations that refute obstinacy; and of it there is a logical kind, in which correct conclusions are drawn from true premises. In the verse before us, the way the conclusion is drawn from the two premises is to say: the disbelievers will never enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle; and the camel will never pass through the eye of the needle; therefore they will never enter Paradise — because making a condition depend on something impossible entails the impossibility of what is conditioned. Much of it will occur in the Noble Qur'an.

The dialectical method in poetry:
This figure has occurred in much Arabic poetry, and they have masterpieces in it. Among them are the words of Abū Tammām:
وإذا أراد الله نشر فضيلة ... طويت أتاح لها لسان حسود
لولا اشتعال النار فيما جاورت ... ما كان يعرف طيب عرف العود
(When Allah wishes to spread a hidden virtue, He provides for it the tongue of an envier; were it not for the fire blazing in what is next to it, the fragrance of aloeswood would not be known.)
The following piece by Bahāʾ al-Dīn Zuhayr is full of varieties of this figure, and we content ourselves with quoting it:
يا من أكابد فيه ما أكابده ... مولاي أصبر حتى يحكم الله
سمّيت غيرك محبوبي مغالطة ... لمعشر فيك قد فاهوا بما فاهوا أقول زيد، وزيد لست أعرفه ... وإنما هو لفظ أنت م
عناه وكم ذكرت مسمّى لا اكتراث به ... حتى يجرّ إلى ذكراك ذ
كراه أتيه فيك على العشاق كلهم ... قد عزّ من أنت يا مولاي
مولاه والناس فينا ببعض القول قد لهجوا ... لو صحّ ما ذكروا ما كنت
آباه كادت عيونهم بالبغض تنطق لي ... حتى كأنّ عيون الناس أفواه
[Translator's note: the line breaks of these verses are disordered in the source and are reproduced as found.]
(O you for whom I endure what I endure, my master, I will be patient until Allah judges. I called someone other than you my beloved, to mislead people who have said what they said about you: I say "Zayd", and Zayd I do not know — it is only a word whose meaning is you. How often I mention someone named for whom I care nothing, until mentioning him leads to mentioning you. I am proud over all lovers because of you: mighty is he whose master you are, my master. People have prattled about us with certain talk; were what they said true, I would not refuse it. Their eyes almost spoke to me with hatred, until it was as if people's eyes were mouths.)
All the reasons mentioned within these verses are genuine, original reasons that the stubborn opponent accepts on hearing them without dispute and without resorting to obstinacy and haughtiness; and that is not hidden from anyone with a grain of taste.

* Benefits:
1- Substitution of the tāʾ:
In ادّكر there are two aspects [Translator's note: so in the source; the word under discussion is ادّاركوا]. The first: the origin is تداركوا, as we mentioned in the Vocabulary section. Whatever has as its first radical a thāʾ, dhāl, dāl, zāy, ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ or ẓāʾ, on the pattern تفاعل, تفعّل or تفعلل, such that the tāʾ and one of these letters come together, the tāʾ is replaced by a letter of the same kind as what follows it and assimilated into it, e.g. اثّاقل، ادّكر، ازّيّن، اصّبر، اضّرع، اطّرب، اظّلم [Translator's note: the source prints «اصتبر»], whose origins are تثاقل، تذكّر، تزيّن، تصبّر، تضرّع، تطرّب، تظلّم. The tāʾ was replaced by a letter of the same kind as what follows it, then made quiescent to be assimilated. Beginning with a quiescent letter being impossible, the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was brought in to escape that.
The second: when the tāʾ of افتعل is changed into a letter homogeneous with what follows it, in stating the pattern one pronounces the original tāʾ of iftiʿāl and not what it has become, ṭāʾ or dāl. So we say the pattern of اصطبر is افتعل, not افطعل, and the pattern of ازدجر is افتعل, not افدعل. Likewise we say here that the pattern of ادّاركوا is اتفاعلوا, not افّاعلوا; there is no difference in this between the tāʾ of iftiʿāl and that of tafāʿul.

2- The defective (manqūṣ) plural on the pattern مفاعل:
The grammarians have two views on a plural on the pattern مفاعل when it is manqūṣ. Some said: it is fully declinable (munṣarif), because the form of the ultimate plural pattern (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ) has left it, so its pattern has become that of جناح; [the cause] has gone, so it is declined. The majority said:
it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), and the tanwīn is a tanwīn of compensation (ʿiwaḍ); this was discussed before.
They differed over what it compensates for. The majority hold that it compensates for the omitted yāʾ; al-Mubarrad held that it compensates for its vowel, and the kasra is not a kasra of i'rab.

dervis-irab:42-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الوسع), with all three vowels on the wāw: capacity. One says: «ليس في وسعه أن يفعل كذا», i.e. he is not able to do it. Al-Zajjāj said: الوسع is what one is able to do.
(الغل): rancour.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ) Resumptive speech introduced to begin mentioning the promise to the believers and what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter, after mentioning the threat to the disbelievers and what has been prepared for them in the Hereafter. The relative noun is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila. (لا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها) The clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya) between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar (predicate). The parenthesis is fitting here because it is of the same kind as the speech: when He, the Exalted, made mention of their righteous deeds, He stated that those deeds are within their capacity and ability and do not go beyond the range of their power. لا is negating; نكلف is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "نحن"; نفسا is the first object of نكلف; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); وسعها is the second object of نكلف. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) The nominal sentence is the khabar of الذين; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب الجنة its khabar; هم is a mubtadaʾ and خالدون its khabar; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) His word خالدون; the clause هم فيها خالدون is a second khabar of أولئك, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أصحاب الجنة. (وَنَزَعْنا ما فِي صُدُورِهِمْ مِنْ غِلٍّ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهارُ) The wāw is a conjunction; نزعنا is a verb and its agent; ما is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في صدورهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted ṣila of the relative; من غلّ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause تجري is a ḥāl of the pronoun. (وَقالُوا: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي هَدانا لِهذا) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a verb and its agent; الحمد is a mubtadaʾ; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the nominal sentence is in the position of the accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of speech); الذي is a relative noun, a naʿt (adjective) of لله; the clause هدانا لهذا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَما كُنَّا لِنَهْتَدِيَ لَوْلا أَنْ هَدانَا اللَّهُ) The wāw may be resumptive or circumstantial; ما is negating; كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); نهتدي is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām of denial; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. لولا is a particle of impossibility due to existence (ḥarf imtināʿ li-wujūd); أن is maṣdariyya, and it together with what it governs is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ being omitted, as the rule states:
وبعد لولا غالبا حذف الخبر ... حتم وفي نص يمين ذا استقر
(After لولا, usually, omission of the khabar is obligatory, and in an explicit oath this is established.)
The apodosis of لولا is omitted because what precedes indicates it; the implied sense is: were it not that Allah's guidance of us exists, we would not have been guided, or we would have been wretched. The whole sentence is resumptive or circumstantial. (لَقَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنا بِالْحَقِّ) The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); جاءت رسل ربنا is a verb and its agent; بالحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءت. (وَنُودُوا أَنْ تِلْكُمُ الْجَنَّةُ أُورِثْتُمُوها بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; نودوا is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); أن may be lightened from the heavy [أنّ] or explicative (mufassira). In تلكم الجنة the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and الجنة is the khabar, or a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative with the khabar being the clause أورثتموها; on the first [view] the clause أورثتموها is circumstantial. The i'rab of the like of بما كنتم تعملون has been given many times before.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المص): A detailed discussion of the openings of the surahs has already been given in Sūrat al-Baqara. We now add to it what al-Suyūṭī mentioned in one of his reports, the gist of which is that these letters are the sound of revelation when it first came down upon the Prophet ﷺ. The well-known words for calling attention, such as ألا and أما, were not used because they are among the words people are accustomed to in their speech, and the Qur'an is speech unlike any speech, so it was fitting that it should bring words of calling attention that were not familiar, so as to strike the ears more effectively. He also mentioned that when the Arabs heard the Qur'an they would make noise over it, so Allah revealed this marvellous arrangement so that they would wonder at it, and their wonder at it would be a way of winning them over, and their listening to it a way of listening to what comes after it, so that hearts would soften and souls become tender. In what al-Suyūṭī mentioned there is much sound judgement and fine insight, for the soul is more cheerful towards what is astonishing, and more eager for what is sudden and not familiar or customary.

* I'rab:
(المص كِتابٌ أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ فَلا يَكُنْ فِي صَدْرِكَ حَرَجٌ مِنْهُ): المص:
The i'rab of the openings of the surahs has been given in Sūrat al-Baqara, so refresh your acquaintance with it. كتاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is a Book"; the clause أنزل إليك is an adjective (ṣifa) of كتاب, and إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل. The ف is a conjunction serving to emphasise the intensity of the prohibition of the الجرح [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for «الحرج» (constraint)], which here is doubt and wavering. Prohibiting the cause is prohibiting the effect by way of demonstration, so what is meant is to forbid him what produces constraint. لا is prohibitive, and يكن is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; في صدرك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of يكن, placed first, and حرج is its noun placed after it. منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of حرج, and the preposition من is causal. (لِتُنْذِرَ بِهِ وَذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The لام is causal, and تنذر is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزل, and به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنذر. ذكرى: it may be conjoined to «لتنذر»; its being accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) is excluded because its time differs from the time of what it gives the reason for, and because the agent differs: the agent of the sending down is Allah, and the agent of the warning is the Prophet. It may be conjoined to the position of «لتنذر», on the model of conjoining an explicit ḥāl (circumstantial) to an interpreted ḥāl, as in His saying the Exalted: «... دعانا لجنبه أو قاعدا أو قائما». «ذكرى» may also be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or by conjunction to «كتاب». Abū al-Baqāʾ erred and allowed it to be a ḥāl; this is not permissible because the و enters upon an explicit ḥāl. It may also be genitive by conjunction to the maṣdar interpreted from the implied أن and the verb, the implied form being: "for the sending down and the reminding".
The Kufans said: it is genitive by conjunction to the pronoun in «به». للمؤمنين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ذكرى. (اتَّبِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) A resumptive statement, set forth to address those legally responsible in general, and the unbelievers in particular, as evidenced by His saying: ولا تتبعوا من دونه أولياء. اتبعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the ن, and the و is the fāʿil (agent); ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; إليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل, and من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl of the relative noun. (وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ قَلِيلًا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ) The و is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تتبعوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا. من دونه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تتبعوا, or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of أولياء and was placed before it. أولياء is a direct object. قليلا is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a little remembrance", or an adjective of a time, i.e. "a little time"; ما is redundant (mazīda), to go deep in emphasising the littleness. تذكرون: originally تتذكرون, an imperfect verb from which one of its two ت's has been dropped; the sign of its nominative is the retention of the ن, and the و is the agent.

dervis-irab:44-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العوج) with kasra on the ʿayn: [crookedness] in abstract things and in concrete things that are not upright; with fatḥa: in things that stand upright, such as a spear or a wall. Further discussion of this root will come.
(الْأَعْرافِ): a wall set up between Paradise and the Fire; they are its heights. It is the plural of عُرف, borrowed from the comb of the cock and the mane of the horse. The authors of the long works have described it at length, and some of them brought the views on it to thirteen.
As for the root ع ر ف, it is remarkable, and we mention here some of its properties and meanings, in keeping with what we have aimed at in this book. One says عرف الشيء يعرفه, of the pattern of ضرب, عرفة, عرفانا and معرفة: he knew it. عرف يعرُف with ḍamma, of the pattern of نصر, عرافة على القوم: he managed them and administered their affairs. عرُف يعرُف with ḍamma in the past and the imperfect, عرافة: he became an ʿarīf (overseer); and [عرف also means] he used much perfume. Among the borrowed usages: the أعراف of the wind, the clouds and the fog, for their front parts; اعرورف البحر: its waves rose high; اعرورف فلان للشر: he craned towards it; and a عرفاء hilltop is a high one. Zuhayr said:
ومرقبة عرفاء أوفيت مقصرا ... لأستأنس الأشباح فيه وأنظرا
(Many a high lookout I have climbed at evening, to make out the figures and to watch.)
مقصرا is from القصر, which is the late afternoon (al-ʿashiyy). العرّاف is lower than the soothsayer (kāhin); they said: «إذا سال بك الغراف لم ينفعك العراف» (when the torrent sweeps you away, the diviner will not help you). And ʿUrwa said:
جعلت لعرّاف اليمامة حكمه ... وعرّاف نجد إذ هما شفياني
(I gave the diviner of al-Yamāma his fee, and the diviner of Najd, if the two would cure me.)
(السّيمى), and السّيمة, السّومة, السّيماء and السيمياء: the mark, the appearance, the radiance and the beauty.

* I'rab:
