2256 - When the grey doves sing, it stirs me (hayyajanī) ... even if I had consoled myself about her, Umm ʿAmmār,
and by "al-Kitāb" the book of Sībawayh, which is a proper name by predominance among the people of this craft. The fifth, which is the most apt and the most deeply into the subtleties of the Quran: that Mūsā, peace be upon him, immerses himself in describing himself as truthful on that occasion, especially since it is reported that when Mūsā said to Pharaoh, may Allah curse him: 'I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds', he said to him: 'You lie', so he says: 'I am bound upon saying the truth', i.e. saying the truth is necessary for me, that I be the one saying it and standing by it, and only one like me is content to speak it." The Shaykh said: "This view is valid only if he means that «أن لا أقول» is a ṣifa of him, as you say 'I am on the saying of the truth', i.e. my way and my habit is saying the truth.
The sixth: «على» is attached to «رسول». Ibn Miqsam said: «حقيق» is of the naʿt of «رسول», i.e. 'a messenger, worthy, from the Lord of the worlds, sent on the condition that I say about Allah only the truth'; this is a sound and clear meaning, and most of the exegetes among the linguists overlooked attaching «على» to «رسول», and it did not occur to them to attach it except to «حقيق»."
The Shaykh said: "His statement has an apparent contradiction, because he first implied «أرسلت» as the operator in «على», and finally said 'because they overlooked attaching «على» to «رسول»'. As for this last, it is not permissible according to the Basrans, because «رسول» has been described before taking its object, and that is not permitted; as for attaching it to an implied «أرسلت», indicated by the word «رسول», it is a permissible implication. His statement is to be interpreted as meaning, by his saying 'attached to «رسول»', that since it indicates it, attributing attachment to it is valid." I say: Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma said, after mentioning this view from Ibn Miqsam: "And the four views of al-Zamakhsharī; but these are forced views, and the meaning is only what I mentioned first, i.e. Ibn Miqsam's view, and this has the difficulty that the Shaykh mentioned, of the active participle, or what runs like it, operating while being described.
Nāfiʿ's reading is clear and has three views. One: the speech is complete at His words «حقيق», with «عليَّ» a fronted khabar and «أنْ لا أقول» a delayed mubtadaʾ, as though it were said: "Upon me is not saying other than the truth", i.e. "so I say only the truth". The second: «حقيق» is a fronted khabar and «أن لا أقول» a mubtadaʾ, as explained. The third: «أَنْ لا أقول» is the fāʿil of «حقيق», as though it were said: "It is due and necessary that I not say"; and this is the clearest of the views for its clarity in wording and meaning; and on the last two views «عليَّ» is attached to «حقيق», since you say "ḥaqqa ʿalayhi kadhā". The Exalted said: {أولئك الذين حَقَّ عليهم القولُ}. On the first view it is attached to an omitted word, as is known more than once.
As for the nominative of «حقيق», it has been stated that it may be a fronted khabar, and it may be a ṣifa of «رسول»; on this it is weak for «مِنْ رب» to be a ṣifa, so as not to necessitate putting a non-explicit ṣifa before an explicit one, so it ought to be attached to «رسول» itself, with «مِنْ» for figurative beginning of the extent.
It may be a second khabar.
It may be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as khabar, according to the reading of whoever intensified the yāʾ, and what justified an indefinite as mubtadaʾ then is the attachment of the preposition and its genitive noun to it.
So four views have been gathered for its nominative; and is it in the sense of fāʿil or in the sense of mafʿūl? The evident view is that it admits both generally, I mean on Nāfiʿ's reading and on the reading of others. Al-Wāḥidī said, relating from others: "With Nāfiʿ's reading it admits both, and with the reading of the majority it is in the sense of mafʿūl", for he said: "ḥaqīq on this reading, meaning Nāfiʿ's reading, may be in the sense of fāʿil. Shamir said: the Arabs say 'ḥaqqa ʿalayya an afʿala kadhā'. Al-Layth said: ḥaqqa l-shayʾ means it became obligatory, and 'it is due upon you to do it', and 'ḥaqīq ʿalayya an afʿalahu'; so this is in the sense of fāʿil", then he said: "Al-Layth said: ḥaqīq is in the sense of mafʿūl, and on this you say: 'so-and-so is maḥqūq ʿalayhi to do'. Al-Aʿshā said:
2257 - She is indeed bound to respond to his voice ... and to know that the one helped is granted success.
And Jarīr said:
2258 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... Fall short, for you, by falling short, are deserving."
Then he said: "and ḥaqīq on this reading, meaning the reading of the majority, is in the sense of maḥqūq." End.
Ubayy read «بَأَنْ لا أقول», and this strengthens that «على» is in the sense of the bāʾ. ʿAbd Allāh and al-Aʿmash read «أنْ لا أقول» without a preposition, so it is possible that the preposition is «على» as in the reading of the majority, and that the preposition is the bāʾ as in Ubayy's reading.
«الحقَّ» may be a direct object because it implies the sense of "he charged him with", and may be accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. "the saying of the truth"; and the exception is vacated.

semin-durr:107-107.t:
His words, the Exalted: {فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ}: «إذا» is the sudden one (fujāʾiyya). It has already been stated that it has three schools: a ẓarf of place, or of time, or a particle. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "idhā is a ẓarf of place in this passage according to al-Mubarrad, in that it is a khabar about a body, while the sound view, held by the people, is that it is a ẓarf of time everywhere." I say: what is well known among the people is the statement of al-Mubarrad, and it is the school of Sībawayh. As for its being time, that is the school of al-Riyāshī, and it is also attributed to Sībawayh. As for his words "in that it is a khabar about a body", it is not here a khabar about a body; rather the khabar of «هي» is the word «ثعبان», not the word «إذا».
Al-thuʿbān is the large male of snakes. Its derivation is from thaʿabtu l-makān, i.e. I made it burst with water; it was likened, in its gliding, to the gliding of water. One says thaʿabtu l-māʾ, I made it burst forth, and it burst forth (inthaʿaba). From it comes mathʿab al-maṭar. In the ḥadīth: "He will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound gushing (yathʿabu) blood." Here there is a question and its answer: He described it once as a thuʿbān, which is the huge, fearsome in creation, and in another place by His words {كَأَنَّهَا جَآنٌّ} [النمل: 10], while al-jānn among snakes is the light, slender in creation; so how are these two attributes combined? Al-Zamakhsharī answered elsewhere than this place with two answers. One: that it combined for it the two things: the largeness of body like the thuʿbān and the lightness of movement and speed of going like the jānn. The second: that at the beginning of its affair it is like the jānn, then grows and its creation increases until it becomes a thuʿbān.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His words, the Exalted: {لِلنَّاظِرِينَ}: attached to an omitted word, because it is a ṣifa of «بيضاء». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: to what is «للناظرين» attached? I say: it is attached to «بيضاء», and the meaning is: 'and lo, it is white for the onlookers', and it is not white for the onlookers except when its whiteness is wondrous, beyond the ordinary, such that people gather to look at it as onlookers gather for marvels." What Abū l-Qāsim mentioned is an interpretation of meaning, not an interpretation of grammatical analysis, and how could he intend a grammatical analysis? He only intended semantic attachment, not technical, like their saying: this speech is attached to that speech, i.e. it is a completion of the meaning for it. And he said in this sūra:
{قَالَ الملأ}

semin-durr:109-109.t:
{قَالَ الملأ}: so he attributed the saying to them. In al-Shuʿarāʾ: «قال للملأ», so he attributed the saying to Pharaoh. Al-Zamakhsharī answered that with three views. One: that this speech issued from him and from them, so here he related it from them and in al-Shuʿarāʾ from him. The second: that he said it originally and his close circle took it from him and said it to those after them. The third: that they said it on his behalf to the people by way of conveying, as kings do: one of them forms an opinion and conveys it to his close circle, then they convey it to the common people. This third is close to the second in meaning.
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read here and in Yūnus: «بكل سَحَّارٍ», and the rest «بكل ساحر». There is no disagreement that what is in al-Shuʿarāʾ is «بكل سَحَّارٍ». Sāḥir and saḥḥār are like ʿālim and ʿallām, and it is known that the pattern faʿʿāl is a pattern of intensification. What favours «سَحَّار» is that it goes beyond «عليم», both being patterns of intensification. What favours «ساحر» is that the like of it preceded in His words «إنَّ هذا لساحر», and this is in keeping with it.

semin-durr:110-110.t:
In al-Shuʿarāʾ: «بسحره», and here without «ذلك». They said: because the beginning of this verse is built on brevity.
His words: {فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ}: the discussion of «ماذا» has already preceded at the beginning of this work. The majority read «تأمرون» with fatḥa on the nūn. Kardam narrated from Nāfiʿ a kasra on it. On both readings «ماذا» as a whole may be a single noun in the position of accusative as the second object of «تأمرون» after the omission of the yāʾ, with the first object of «تأمرون» omitted, namely the speaker's yāʾ, the implied form being: "With what do you command me?" On Nāfiʿ's reading, you do not say that the first object is omitted; rather it is in the force of the pronounced one, because the kasra indicates it, so this omission is not the omission in the reading of the majority. It is possible that «ما» is interrogative in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and «ذا» a relative with the ṣila «تأمرون», and the returning pronoun omitted, and the first object also omitted on the reading of the majority; the returning pronoun implied is accusative in position, not transitivized to it with the bāʾ, so its implied form is: "What is it that you command me (tamurūnanīhi)?" Ibn ʿAṭiyya implied it as «تأمروني به», and the Shaykh objected to him, that this necessitates omitting a returning pronoun governed by a preposition by which the relative is not governed, then excused him, saying that he intended the original implication, and then latitude was taken in it so that the preposition was omitted and the pronoun attached to the verb. Is this clause part of the speech of the chiefs, who thus addressed Pharaoh alone out of honour for him, as kings are addressed in the plural form; or did they say it to him and to his companions; or is it from the speech of Pharaoh, on the implication of a saying, i.e. "Pharaoh said to them: so what do you command?" What supports its being from Pharaoh's speech is His words, the Exalted: «قالوا: أرْجِهْ».
Is «تأمرون» from the familiar command (amr), or from the amr which means consultation? The second is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from amartuhu, so he amaranī bi-kadhā, i.e. I consulted him and he advised me an opinion."

semin-durr:177-177.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَآءَ مَثَلاً}: «ساء» has the meaning of «بئس» ("evil is"), and its agent is a latent pronoun in it, and «مثلاً» is a tamyīz (specification) explaining it. It has been mentioned more than once that the agent in this chapter, when it is a pronoun, is explained by what follows it, and the dual, plural and feminine of it are dispensed with, by dualising, pluralising and feminising the specification, according to the Basrans. It was also mentioned that «ساء» originally takes an object, and that the one specified for censure (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) can only be of the genus of the specification, / and the specification explains the agent, so it is the same as it; so it is necessary that the agent, the specification and the one specified for censure be true of one and the same thing. If this is known, then His saying «القوم» is not true of the specification and the agent; hence an omitted element must be supposed, either in the specification or in the one specified for censure. In the first it is supposed: "evil are the people of a likeness" or "the people of the likeness of the people"; in the second it is supposed: "evil as a likeness is the likeness of the people"; then the muḍāf was omitted in both suppositions and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place; and this clause is an emphasis of the one before it.
Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «ساء مثلُ القوم» with «مثل» nominative, annexed to «القوم». And it is reported from al-Jaḥdarī likewise, and it is reported from him with kasra on the mīm, sukūn on the thāʾ, ḍamma on the lām and genitive «القوم». This reading ascribed to this group admits of two views. One: that «ساء» is for wonder, indeclinable in implication on the pattern faʿula with ḍamma on the ʿayn, like their saying «لقَضُو الرجل», and «مثل القوم» is its agent, the implied form being: "How evil is the likeness of the people!", and the relative noun on this view is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «قوم». The second: that it has the meaning of «بئس», and «مَثَلُ القوم» is the agent, and the relative noun on this is in the position of nominative because it is the one specified for censure, and on this an omitted muḍāf is necessary so that the agent and the one specified are true of the same thing; the implied form being: "evil is the likeness of the people, the likeness of those who…". The Shaykh supposed a specification in this reading, and there is an objection in this, since no specification is needed when the agent is overt, to the point that they made combining the two a necessity (of poetry), as in his saying:
2340 - تَزوَّدْ مثلَ زادِ أبيك فينا ... فنعمَ الزَّادُ زادُ أبيك زادا
(Take provisions like your father's provisions among us; how excellent a provision is your father's provision, as provision!)
And there are three positions on the question: permissible absolutely; prohibited absolutely; and the distinction: if it is different from the wording and gives a new benefit it is permitted, such as «نعم الرجل شجاعاً زيد», and on this is his saying:
2341 - تخيَّرَهُ فلم يَعْدِلْ سواه ... فنِعْمَ المرءُ مِنْ رجلٍ تَهامي
(He chose him and did not prefer another; how excellent a man — a man of Tihāma!)
His saying: {وَأَنفُسَهُمْ كَانُواْ يَظْلِمُونَ}: an object of «يظلمون», and in it is evidence for putting the khabar of kāna before it, because putting the object first indicates putting the governor first, generally. I said "generally" because there are places where that is prohibited, such as {فَأَمَّا اليتيم فَلاَ تَقْهَرْ} [al-Ḍuḥā: 9]: «اليتيم» is an object of «تقهر», and it is not permissible to put «تقهر» before its jussive-governing particle; and this is open to discussion.
This kāna-clause admits of two views. One: that it is conjoined to the ṣila, which is «كَذَّبوا بآياتنا». The second: that it is resumptive; on both sayings it has no position; the object was put first to give exclusivity, and this follows the way of al-Zamakhsharī and his peers.

semin-durr:178-178.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَن يَهْدِ الله فَهُوَ المهتدي}: it took into account the wording of «مَنْ» and so used the singular, and took into account its meaning in His saying «أولئك هم الخاسرون» and so used the plural. The yāʾ of «المهتدي» is retained by all the readers because it is retained in the script; a disagreement concerning the one in al-Isrāʾ and a discussion of it will come to you. Al-Wāḥidī said: "«فهو المهتدي»: retaining the yāʾ is permissible on the basis of the original, and dropping it is permissible for lightness, as was said in the verse of the Book [Translator's note: i.e., Sībawayh's Kitāb]:
2342 - فَطِرْتُ بمُنْصُلي في يَعْمَلات ... دوامي الأَيْدِ يَخْبِطْنَ السَّريحا
(So I sped with my sword among swift she-camels, bloody-handed [in their forelegs], striking the leather thong.)
and from it:
2343 - كنَواحِ ريشِ حَمامةٍ نَجْديةِ ... ومَسَحْتَ باللِّثتين عَصْفَ الإِثْمِدِ
(Like the wing-feathers of a Najdī dove, and you wiped the gums with the stalks of kohl.)
Ibn Jinnī said: 'He likened the muḍāf ilayhi to tanwīn, so he dropped the yāʾ for it.'"

semin-durr:179-179.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لِجَهَنَّمَ}: two views are permissible regarding this lām. One: that it is the lām of outcome and consequence (ṣayrūra and ʿāqiba), and the one who says so needs it to be the lām of consequence only because of His saying, the Exalted {وَمَا خَلَقْتُ الجن والإنس إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُونِ} [al-Dhāriyāt: 56], for this is a considered, restricted reason, so how can this also be a reason? And they adduced the poet's saying: 2344 - لِدُوا للموت وابْنُوا للخراب ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Beget for death and build for ruin…)
and the other's saying:
2345 - ألا كلُّ مولودٍ فللموتِ يُوْلَدُ ... ولستُ أرى حَيّاً لحيٍّ يُخَلَّدُ
(Indeed every one born is born for death, and I see no living being made immortal.)
and the other's saying:
2346 - فللموتِ تَغْذُو الوالداتُ سِخالَها ... كما لخرابِ الدور تُبْنَى المساكنُ
(For death mothers nurture their young, as dwellings are built for the ruin of houses.)
The second: that it is for cause, in that since their end was to it, that was made a cause in the manner of figurative usage.
Ibn ʿAṭiyya rebutted the one who made it the lām of consequence, saying: "This is not correct, and the lām of consequence is conceivable only when the agent's act did not aim at the outcome of the matter being that; but here the act was aimed at what the matter comes to [be] — their dwelling in Hell"; and the lām on this is attached to «ذَرَأْنا». It is also permissible that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «كثيراً», because in origin it is an adjective of it had it come later. There is no need to claim inversion, that the origin is: "We created Hell for many," since that is a necessity or rare.
And {مِّنَ الجن} is an adjective of «كثيراً». «لهم قلوب» is a clause in the position of accusative: either an adjective of «كثير» too, or a ḥāl from «كثيراً» even though it is indefinite, for its being specified by the description; or from the latent pronoun in «من الجن», because it carries / a pronoun by virtue of its being an adjective. It is also permissible that «لهم» alone be the description or the ḥāl, and «قلوب» its agent, so it would be a description with a singular, which is preferable. And His saying: {لاَّ يَفْقَهُونَ بِهَا}, and likewise the negated clause, is in the position of an adjective of what precedes it, and this description is almost necessary — were it to occur in other than the Qurʾān — because there is no benefit without it; if you said «لزيد قَلْبٌ وله عينٌ» and stopped, no great benefit would appear from it.

semin-durr:180-180.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {الحسنى}: two sayings about it. The clearer: that it is the feminine of «أحسن», and the broken plural of a non-rational being may be described by what the feminine is described by, such as «مآرب أخرى»; and had it been made to agree (in the plural), the construction would have been good, as in His saying: {مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ} [al-Baqara: 184]. The second: that «الحسنى» is a maṣdar on the pattern fuʿlā, like al-rujʿā and al-buqyā. He said:
2347 - ولا يَجْزون مِنْ حُسْنى بسوءٍ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And they do not repay a good with evil…)
And «الأسماء» here: the words indicating the Creator, the Exalted, such as «الله» and «الرحمن». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "What is meant by them is the namings (al-tasmiyāt), by the consensus of the interpreters; nothing else is possible." There is an objection in this, because tasmiya is a maṣdar, and a maṣdar is not invoked with, on both sayings in the explanation of invocation; for the meaning of «فادعوه» is "call Him by them," as in their saying: "O Allah, O Raḥmān, O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity, forgive us." It was said: "name Him by them," as you say «سَمَّيْت ابني بزيد».
His saying: {يُلْحِدُونَ}: Ḥamza read here and in al-Naḥl and Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda «يَلْحدون» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ, from laḥada, triliteral. The rest read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ, from alḥada. It was said: they are one in meaning, which is inclining and deviating. From it is laḥd al-qabr (the niche-grave), because it is inclined, by digging it to the side, unlike ḍarīḥ (the central trench-grave), which is dug in the middle; and from their speech: "What has the finder done? They said: the niche-digger (al-lāḥid) niched him." Ibn al-Sikkīt held that they are one in meaning and said: "They are turning away from the truth." And alḥada is used more than laḥada. He said:
2348 - ليس الإِمام بالشحيح المُلْحِدِ
(The imam is not the stingy deviator.)
Another said: "laḥada means 'he leaned and attached himself,' and alḥada: 'he inclined and deviated,'" al-Kisāʾī said so. It was also transmitted from him: alḥada: he turned away; laḥada: he inclined. They said: for this reason Ḥamza agreed in al-Naḥl, since its meaning is: "they incline to him."
Abū ʿUbayda transmitted from al-Aṣmaʿī: "alḥada: he disputed and argued; laḥada: he swerved and inclined." The reading of the majority was preferred by consensus on His saying «بإلحاد». Al-Wāḥidī said: "Lāḥid is scarcely heard from the Arabs." I say: their abstaining from the coming of the active participle of the triliteral indicates its rarity, and I have given earlier from their speech «لحده اللاحِد». The meaning of ilḥād in it is that they derived from them [the divine names] names for their gods, so they say: al-Lāt from the word «الله», al-ʿUzzā from the word «العزيز», and Manāt from the word «المَنَّان»; and it is possible that what is meant is that they named Him with what does not befit His majesty.

semin-durr:181-181.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِمَّنْ خَلَقْنَآ أُمَّةٌ}: «مَنْ» may be a relative noun or a qualified indefinite, and «يَهْدون» is an adjective of «أمة». Some of them said: "There is an omission in the speech, its implied form being: 'and of those We created for Paradise,' which is indicated by what is established for their counterparts, namely His saying: {وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ} [al-ʿArāf: 179]." [Translator's note: the source gives the sūra name as «العراف»; it is al-Aʿrāf.]

semin-durr:149-149.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سُقِطَ في أَيْدِيهِمْ}: The preposition phrase stands in the place of the agent. It is also said: what stands in the place of [the agent] is the pronoun of the maṣdar, which is السُّقوط, i.e. "falling fell in their hands". The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) reported from some that he said: "«سقط» implies an object, which here is the maṣdar, i.e. الإِسقاط, as in your saying «ذُهب بزيد»." He said: "The right form is: it is here the pronoun of the maṣdar which is السُّقوط, because the maṣdar of «سقط» is not الإِسقاط, and because what stands in the place of the agent is the pronoun of the maṣdar and not the maṣdar." al-Wāḥidī reported from al-Azharī that their saying «سُقِط في يده» is like the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

2294 - دَعْ عنك نَهْباً صِيح في حُجُراتِه ... ولكنْ حديثاً ما حديث الرواحلِ
(Leave aside plunder cried out in its precincts, but tell me — what is the tale of the riding camels?)

in that the verb is attributed to the preposition phrase, as if it were said: "the plunderer cried out in its precincts"; and likewise what is meant is «سُقِط في يده», i.e. "regret fell in his hand." I say: his saying "i.e. regret fell" is an explicit statement that what stands in the place of the agent is the preposition, not the pronoun of the maṣdar. al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj reported that one says سُقِط في يده and also أُسقط, except that al-Farrāʾ said: "سَقَط, i.e. the triliteral, is more frequent and better." This expression is used for remorse and bewilderment.

The statements of the lexicographers about its origin were confused. Abū Marwān Ibn Sirāj, the lexicographer, said: "The saying of the Arabs سُقِط في يده is among what has defeated me as to its meaning." al-Wāḥidī said: "It is clear from the statements of the exegetes and the lexicographers that «سُقِط في يده» means 'he regretted', and that it is used in describing the remorseful. As for the account of its origin and what defines it, I have seen nothing from the leading authorities of the language that I accept, except what al-Zajjājī mentioned, for he said: 'His saying, the Exalted, «سُقِط في أيديهم» in the sense of "they regretted" is a composition not heard before the Quran and not known to the Arabs, and it is not found in their poetry. What proves the soundness of that is that when the poets of Islam heard this composition and used it in their speech, the manner of its use was hidden from them, because their habit did not run to it, and Abū Nuwās said:

2295 - ونشوةٌ سُقِطْتُ منها في يدي ...
(And an intoxication from which I was "fallen" into my hand…)

Abū Nuwās is the master-scholar, yet he erred in using this expression, because فُعِلْتُ is formed only from a transitive verb, and «سَقَط» is intransitive and does not become transitive except with a preposition; one does not say «سُقطت», just as one does not say رُغبت or غُضِبت; one says only رُغِب في and غُضِب على. Abū Ḥātim mentioned that «سُقِط فلان في يده» means "he regretted", and this is an error like the saying of Abū Nuwās; had it been so, the composition would have been «ولما سُقطوا في أيديهم» and «سُقِط القومُ في أيديهم». Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is said of one who has regretted a matter and is powerless over it: سُقِط في يده."'"

al-Wāḥidī said: "The mention of the hand here is for two reasons. One: it is said of whatever comes about, even if it is something that cannot be in the hand, 'something disagreeable has come into his hand', likening what occurs in the soul and heart to what is seen with the eye; and the hand is singled out for mention because the committing of sins is by it, so the blame returns to it as it is the principal limb, and so is attributed to it what it did not itself do, as in {ذلك بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاكَ} [al-Ḥajj: 10], though many sins were not put forward by the hand. The second: that regret is an event occurring in the heart whose trace appears in the hand, for the regretful bites his hand and strikes one hand against the other, as in {فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ} [al-Kahf: 42], where turning over the palms is an expression for regret, and as in {وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظالم على يَدَيْهِ} [al-Furqān: 27]. So since the trace of regret occurs in the hand in the way we mentioned, the falling of regret was attributed to the hand; for what appears to the eyes of the act of the regretful is the turning over of the palm and the biting of the fingers and hand, just as joy is a meaning in the heart that a person senses, and what appears of it is the state of stirring, movement, laughter and the like."

al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولمَّا سُقِط في أيديهم» means: when their regret grew intense, because it is the way of one whose regret and anguish are intense to bite his hand in grief so that his hand becomes something fallen into, since his mouth has fallen into it." It is also said: it is the habit of the regretful to lower his head and rest his chin on his hand, leaning on it, and to be in a posture such that if his hand were removed he would fall on his face, so it is as if the hand is fallen into. The meaning of «في» is «على», so the meaning of «في أيديهم» is "upon their hands", like {وَلأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِي جُذُوعِ النخل} [Ṭā Hā: 71]. It is also said: it is taken from السِّقاط, which is abundant error, and the one who errs regrets his deed. Ibn Abī Kāhil said:

2296 - كيف يَرْجُون سِقاطي بعدما ... لَفَّع الراسَ بياضٌ وصَلَعْ
(How can they hope for my slip after whiteness and baldness have wrapped my head?)

It is also said: it is taken from السَّقيط, which is the frost that covers the ground, resembling snow; from it one says سَقَطَت الأرض as one says ثَلَجت; the سَقْط and سَقيط melt at the least warmth and do not remain, and one into whose hand the frost falls obtains nothing from it, so this became a proverb for everyone who loses in his outcome and gains nothing of value from his aim.

Know that «سُقِطَ في يده» was counted by some among the verbs that are not conjugated, like نِعْمَ and بئس. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «سَقَط في أيديهم», active, its agent latent, i.e. "regret fell"; this is the view of al-Zajjāj. al-Zamakhsharī said: "the biting fell." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "loss and disappointment fell"; and all of these are examples. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أُسْقِط», quadriliteral, passive. It has already been mentioned that it is a dialect reported by al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj.

His saying: {وَرَأَوْاْ أَنَّهُمْ}: this is of the heart, and in this there is no need for preposing and postposing as some claimed. He said: "its implied form: when they saw that they had gone astray and regret fell in their hands," saying "because regret and anguish occur only after knowledge."

His saying: {لَئِن لَّمْ يَرْحَمْنَا}: the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza) read «ترحمنا وتغفر» in the second person, and «ربَّنا» accusative. This is the reading of al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Wathāb, Ibn Muṣarrif, al-Jaḥdarī, al-Aʿmash and Ayyūb; and the rest of the seven read with the third-person yāʾ in both, and «ربُّنا» nominative, which is the reading of al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Aʿraj, Shayba and Abū Jaʿfar. The accusative is as a vocative, and the second person suits it; the nominative is as an agent. It is possible that this speech came from all of them in succession, or that this was from one group and that from another group: whoever was overcome by fear and was strong enough to face Him addressed Him, asking release from his sin; and whoever was overcome by shame put his speech in the manner of one shy of addressing, so he attributed the verb to the absent.

semin-durr:150-150.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {غَضْبَانَ أَسِفاً}: two ḥāls from Moses according to those who allow multiple ḥāls; and according to those who do not, «أَسِفاً» is made a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «غضبان», so it is a nested ḥāl, or it is made a badal from the first. There is something to consider in this, for the difficulty of fitting it into the categories of badal; the nearest thing said is that it is a badal of part from whole (badal baʿḍ min kull) if we explain الأَسِف as intensely angry, or a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) if we explain it as sorrowful. One says أسِف يأسَفُ أَسَفاً, i.e. his anger became intense. The Exalted said: {فَلَمَّآ آسَفُونَا انتقمنا مِنْهُمْ} [al-Zukhruf: 55]. It is also said: rather its meaning is "sorrowful," and from it is the saying:

2297 - غيرُ مأسوفٍ على زمنٍ ... ينقضي بالهمِّ والحزن
(Not to be regretted is a time that passes away in worry and sorrow.)

Since the two are close in meaning, the badal is sound as I mentioned to you; and what shows the closeness between them, as al-Wāḥidī said, is the saying:

2298 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
فحزنُ كلِّ أخي حُزْنٍ أخو الغضبِ
(… [first half elided in the source] … for the grief of every man of grief is the brother of anger.)

and al-Aʿshā said:

2299 - أرى رجلاً منكمْ أسِيفاً كأنما ... يَضُمُّ إلى كَشْحَيْه كَفَّاً مُخَضَّبا
(I see a man among you, angry/grieved, as if he were pressing to his flanks a dyed hand.)

This is in the sense of "angry". And in the ḥadīth: «إنَّ أبا بكر رجلٌ أسيف», i.e. sorrowful; and رجلٌ أَسِف is used when the permanence and settledness of the attribute is intended; if time is intended by it, it comes on فاعِل.

His saying: {قَالَ: بِئْسَمَا}: this is the apodosis of «لمَّا», and the discussion of «بئسما» has preceded, but the one specified for blame is omitted, and the agent is latent, explained by «ما خَلَفْتموني»; the implied form being: "evil is the succession in which you succeeded me, your succession."

His saying: {أَعَجِلْتُمْ أَمْرَ رَبِّكُمْ}: about «أَمْرَ» there are two views. One: that it is accusative as an object after the dropping of the preposition, and the verb being given the meaning of what takes its object directly; the original: أَعَجِلْتُمْ عن أمر ربكم. al-Zamakhsharī said: "One says عَجِل عن الأمر when he left it incomplete, and its opposite is تَمَّ, and another made him hasten away from it (أعجله عنه); and it is given the meaning of «سبق» (outstrip) so it is transitivised like it, and one says عَجِلْتُ الأمر; and the meaning: did you hasten away from the command of your Lord?" The second: that it is transitive by itself, not given the sense of another verb. Yaʿqūb related: «عَجِلْتُ الشيء» "I outstripped the thing," and أعجلت الرجل "I urged the man to haste," i.e. I made him hurry.

His saying: {يَجُرُّهُ إِلَيْهِ}: three views. One: that the sentence is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun of Moses in «أخذ», i.e. "he took him, dragging him to himself." The second: that it is a ḥāl from «رأس»; so said Abū l-Baqāʾ, and there is something to consider in it because of the lack of a link. The third: that it is a ḥāl from «أخيه»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is weak," meaning because a ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi seldom occurs or is impossible according to some. I say: it has been mentioned more than once that some allow it in cases like this, namely when the muḍāf is a part of the muḍāf ilayhi.

His saying: {قَالَ ابن أُمَّ}: the two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza), Abū Bakr and Ibn ʿĀmir read here and in Ṭā Hā with kasra on the mīm, and the rest with fatḥa. As for the reading with fatḥa, there are two doctrines. The doctrine of the Basrans: that the two are indeclinable on fatḥa because of their being compounded like خمسة عشر; on this «ابن» is not annexed to «أم» but is compounded with it, so the vowel of the two is a vowel of indeclinability. The second: the doctrine of the Kufans, that «ابن» is annexed to «أُمّ», and «أم» is annexed to the first-person yāʾ, and the yāʾ has been turned into an alif as it is turned in a vocative annexed to the first-person yāʾ, as in يا غلاماً, then the alif was dropped and the fatḥa sufficed for it, as the kasra suffices for the yāʾ; so the vowel of «ابن» is then a case vowel and it is annexed to «أُمَّ», which is in the position of genitive by annexation.

As for the reading with kasra, on the Basran view it is a kasra of indeclinability on account of the first-person yāʾ, in the sense that we annexed this entire compounded noun to the first-person yāʾ, so its end was given kasra, then the kasra sufficed for the yāʾ; it is therefore a parallel to: يا أحَدَ عشري, then يا أحد عَشرِ with omission. It is not possible that they remain in annexation, since dropping the yāʾ is not allowed because the noun is not a vocative, but is annexed to the vocative, so dropping the yāʾ from it is not allowed. On the Kufan view the kasra is a case kasra, and the yāʾ is dropped, the kasra sufficing for it, as the fatḥa sufficed for its alif. These two views apply to «ابن أم», «ابن عم», «ابنة أم» and «ابنة عم». Know that in these four examples specifically, five dialects are allowed, the most eloquent being: dropping the yāʾ with the kasra sufficing for it; then turning the yāʾ into an alif, so the kasra necessarily becomes fatḥa; then dropping the alif with the fatḥa sufficing for it; then retaining the yāʾ quiescent or with fatḥa. As for other than these four examples, of what is annexed to something annexed to the first-person yāʾ in the vocative, only what is allowed in other than the chapter of the vocative is allowed in it, because it is not the one addressed, as in يا غلامَ أبي and يا غلام أمي; these examples specifically took this course only by placing the two words in the position of a single word and because of frequency of use.

«يابن أمي» is also read with the yāʾ retained quiescent, and similar to it is the saying:

2300 - يابنَ أُمِّي ويا شُقَيِّق نفسي ... أنت خَلَّفْتَني لدهرٍ شديدِ
(O son of my mother, O twin of my soul, you left me behind for a harsh time.)

and the saying of another:

2301 - يا بنَ أمي فَدَتْكَ نفسي ومالي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O son of my mother, may my soul and my wealth ransom you … [rest elided in the source])

It is also read «ابن إمِّ» with kasra on the hamza and the mīm, which is imitation of the vowel. And an example of turning the yāʾ into an alif is the saying:

2302 - يا بنة عَمَّا لا تَلُومي واهْجَعي ...
(O daughter of my paternal uncle, do not blame me, and sleep.)

and his saying:

2303 - كُنْ لي لا عَليَّ يا بن عَمَّا ... نَدُمْ عَزِيزَيْنِ ونُكْفَ الذَّمَّا
(Be for me, not against me, O son of my paternal uncle; we shall remain two mighty ones and be spared blame.)

His saying: {فَلاَ تُشْمِتْ}: the majority have ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from أَشْمت, quadriliteral, «الأعداء» being a direct object. Ibn Muḥayṣin read «فلا تَشْمِتْ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the mīm, and Mujāhid with fatḥa on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the mīm, «الأعداءَ» being accusative as a direct object. In these two readings there are two explanations; the more evident: that شمِت or شَمَت, with kasra or fatḥa on the mīm, is transitive by itself like the quadriliteral أشمت; one says شمت بي زيدٌ العدوَّ, as one says أَشْمَتَّ بي العدو.

The second: that «تَشْمت» is attributed to the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. "do not (Yourself) cause gloating, O Lord," and this is allowed as {الله يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ} is allowed, with an implied governor for "the enemies" accusative as in the reading of the group; so said Ibn Jinnī. There is no need for this artifice because the triliteral «شمت» can be transitive by itself, and implication is contrary to the basic rule. Abū l-Baqāʾ said of this explanation: "do not you cause gloating," making the agent the pronoun of Moses, which is preferable to attributing it to the pronoun of Allah the Exalted. As for his likening it to {الله يَسْتَهْزِىءُ بِهِمْ}, that is allowed only for the sake of correspondence in His saying {إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِئُونَ} [al-Baqara: 14], and like {وَمَكَرُواْ وَمَكَرَ الله} [Āl ʿImrān: 54], and it is not allowed apart from correspondence.

Ḥumayd ibn Qays read: «فلا تَشْمِت» like the reading of Ibn Muḥayṣin, and Mujāhid like his reading at first, except that the two made «الأعداء» nominative as agent, making شمت intransitive and so making "the enemies" nominative by it as agent; so the prohibition is in wording addressed to the one addressed, while what is meant by it is someone else, like their saying «لا أُرَيَنَّك ههنا» ("let me not see you here"), i.e. "let there not come from you what requires that the enemies gloat over me."

الإِشمات and الشَّماتة are rejoicing at a calamity that befalls your enemy. He said:

2304 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... والموتُ دون شماتَةِ الأعداء
(… [first half elided in the source] … and death is better than the gloating of enemies.)

It is said: its derivation is from شوامِت الدابة, which are its legs, because gloating turns the heart of the envier between the two states of joy and grief, like the turning about of the legs of the beast. تشميت العاطس and تَسْميته, with shīn and with sīn, is a supplication of good for him; Abū ʿUbayd said: "The shīn is the higher of the two dialects," and Thaʿlab said: "The original in both is the sīn, from السَّمْت, which is directness and guidance." It is also said: the meaning of tashmīt of the sneezer with the dotted letter is that Allah make him firm as He makes firm the legs of the beast. It is also said: rather the pattern تفعيل is for removal, i.e. may Allah remove gloating from him; and with the undotted sīn, i.e. may Allah return him to his first bearing (samt), meaning his form, because he suffers a jolt. Abū Bakr said: "One says سَمَته and سَمَت عليه, and in the ḥadīth: «وسَمَّت عليهما»."

semin-durr:182-182.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والذين كَذَّبُواْ}: two views are permissible. The clearer: that it is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar is the future clause after it. The second view: that it is accusative by occupation (ishtighāl) with an implied verb, its implied form being: "We shall draw gradually (sa-nastadrij) those who denied." Al-istidrāj is drawing near stage by stage and seizing little by little, from al-daraj (the step), because one who ascends climbs step by step, and likewise one who descends. It was said: it is taken from al-darj, which is folding, and from it: "he folded (daraja) the garment," and "he rolled up (daraja) the dead man" is the same. The meaning: their terms are folded up.
Al-Nakhaʿī and Ibn Wathāb read «سَيَسْتَدْرِجُهم» with the yāʾ, which admits that the agent is the Creator, the Exalted, and it is an iltifāt from the first person to the third; and that the agent is the pronoun of denial understood from His saying «كذَّبوا». Al-Aʿshā said, on istidrāj:
2349 - فلو كنتَ في جُبٍّ ثمانين قامةً ... ورُقِّيْتَ أسبابَ السماءِ بسُلَّمِ
لَيَسْتَدْرِجَنْكَ القولُ حتى تَهِرَّهُ ... وتَعْلَمَ أنِّي عنكمُ غيرُ مُلْجَمِ
(Were you in a pit eighty fathoms deep, and were you raised to the ropes of heaven by a ladder, my speech would draw you on until you loathe it, and you would know that I am not bridled against you.)
It is said: "the boy walked haltingly (daraja)" when he shortens his steps, and "the people passed away (daraja)": some of them died after others.

semin-durr:183-183.t: His saying, the Exalted: {وَأُمْلِي}: Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed that it be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "and I grant respite"; that it be resumptive; and that it be conjoined to «سنستدرج». There is an objection in this, since in terms of eloquence, had it been so, [it would have been] «ونُمْلي» with the nūn of magnification. It is also permissible that this be close to an iltifāt. Al-imlāʾ is granting respite and prolonging. Al-matīn is the strong. From it is al-matn, which is the middle, because it is the strongest part of a living creature. Matuna yamtunu matānatan, that is, he became strong. The majority read «إنَّ كيدي» with kasra, as resumptive, indicating overpowering. Ibn ʿĀmir, in the transmission of ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, read «أنَّ كيدي» with fatḥa on the hamza, as a reason.

semin-durr:184-184.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ مَا بِصَاحِبِهِمْ}: several views are permissible regarding «ما». One: that it is interrogative, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «بصاحبهم», that is: "What thing of madness has settled in their companion?" Al-jinna is a maṣdar meaning a state, like al-rikba and al-jilsa. It was said: what is meant by al-jinna is the jinn, as in {مِنَ الجنة والناس}, and then an omitted muḍāf is necessary, that is: "the touch of a jinn" or "the convulsion of a jinn."
The second: that «ما» is negating, that is: "there is no madness in their companion, nor touch of a jinn." Regarding these two clauses — I mean the interrogative or the negated — there are two views. The clearer: that it is in the position of accusative after removal of the preposition, because they suspend (the effect of) reflection, as it is among the verbs of the heart. The second: that the speech is complete at His saying «أو لم يتفكروا», then another speech begins, either an interrogative of denial or a negation. Al-Ḥawfī said: "«ما بصاحبهم» is suspended from an omitted verb indicated by the speech, the implied form being: 'Did they not reflect and so know what is in their companion?'" He said: "And «تفكَّر» is not suspended, because it did not enter upon a clause." This is weak, because they stated that a heart-verb which is transitive by a preposition or to one object, when suspended, does it remain as it was or is it made to include [the meaning of] what takes two objects?
The third: that «ما» is relative, meaning «الذي», the implied form being: "Did they not reflect on that which is in their companion," and on this the speech came out according to their claim. And on our saying that it is negating, «من جنة» would be a mubtadaʾ with «مِنْ» redundant in it and «بصاحبهم» its khabar, that is: "no madness is in their companion."

semin-durr:185-185.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَأَنْ عسى}: concerning «أنْ» there are two views. One — and it is the correct one — that it is the lightened form of «أنَّ», and its noun is the pronoun of the matter and affair (ḍamīr al-amr wa-l-shaʾn). «عسى» and what falls within its scope is in the position of nominative as its khabar, and no separation is made here between «أنْ» and the khabar even though it is a verb, because the inert verb that is not conjugated resembles nouns; and like it {وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلإِنسَانِ إِلاَّ مَا سعى} [al-Najm: 39] and {والخامسة أَنَّ غَضَبَ الله عَلَيْهَآ} [al-Nūr: 9] in the reading of Nāfiʿ, because it is a supplication. The khabar of «أنْ» occurred as a clause of request in these last two verses, since «عسى» is for inshāʾ (performative) and «غضب الله» is a supplication.
The second: that it is the maṣdar-forming one; Abū l-Baqāʾ said so, meaning the one with two-letter construction that puts the imperfect in the accusative. This is not good, because the grammarians stated that the maṣdar-forming «أنْ» is attached only to a conjugated verb in any form, that is past, imperfect and imperative, and «عسى» is not conjugated, so how can it occur as its ṣila? And «أنْ» on both views is in the position of genitive, conjoined to «ملكوت», that is: "Did they not look into the fact that the matter and affair is that perhaps…". And «أن يكون» is the agent of «عسى», and then it is complete (tāmma), because whenever it takes «أنْ» and what falls under it as its agent it is complete, and like it in that are awshaka and ikhlawlaqa. About the name of «يكون» there are two sayings. One: it is the pronoun of the affair, and «قد اقترب أجلهم» is its khabar. The second: that it is «أجلُهم», and «قد اقترب» is a clause of verb and agent, the agent being the pronoun of «أجلهم»; but the khabar, which is a verbal clause, was put before its noun, and this and the disagreement over it have been given earlier: namely that Ibn Mālik allows it and Ibn ʿUṣfūr prohibits it, at His saying: {مَا كَانَ يَصْنَعُ فِرْعَوْنُ} [al-Aʿrāf: 137].
His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ}: attached to «يُؤْمنون», and it is an interrogative clause brought for wonder, that is: "if they do not believe in this discourse, then how will they believe in any other?" And the hāʾ in «بعده» admits of returning to the Qurʾān and of returning to the Messenger, and then the speech involves an omitted muḍāf, that is: "after his report and his story"; and of returning to «أجلهم», that is: "when they die and their term expires, how will they believe after the expiry of their term?" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: to what do you attach His saying «فبأي حديث بعده يؤمنون»? I say: to His saying «عسى أن يكونَ قد اقترب أجلهم». It is as if it were said: 'perhaps their term has drawn near, so what is the matter with them that they do not hasten [to] belief in the Qurʾān before death, and what are they waiting for after the truth has become clear, and in what discourse more true than it do they wish to believe?'" He means the attachment in meaning, linked to what precedes it, not the technical one, and it is clear.
His saying: «ويَذَرهم»: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read it with the yāʾ and a jussive verb; ʿĀṣim and Abū ʿAmr with the yāʾ also and a nominative verb; Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ibn ʿĀmir with the nūn and a nominative verb also.
The jussive has also been reported from Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr among the irregular readings. The nominative is from one view, which is resumption, that is: "and He leaves them" or "and We leave them," according to the two readings. / As for the sukūn, it admits of two views. One: that it is a jussive conjoined to the position of His saying «فلا هادي له», because the negated clause is the apodosis of the condition and so is in the position of the jussive, so he conjoined to its position; and it is like His saying, the Exalted: {وَإِن تُخْفُوهَا وَتُؤْتُوهَا الفقرآء فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ وَيُكَفِّرُ} [al-Baqara: 271] with «يكفر» jussive, and like the poet's saying:
2350 - أنَّى سلكتَ فإنني لك كاشحٌ ... وعلى انتقاصِك في الحياة وأزْدَدِ
(Wherever you go, I am your enemy, and I am bent on belittling you in life, and I shall increase.)
Al-Wāḥidī also recited the other's saying:
2351 - فَأَبْلوني بَلِيَّتَكمْ لعلِّي ... أُصالِحُكم وأسْتدرِجْ نَوَيَّا
(So try me with your trial, perhaps I shall reconcile with you and draw my intention gradually.)
He said: "«أستدرج» is carried over to the position of the omitted fāʾ from «فلعلي أصالحكم»." The second: that it is a sukūn of lightening, like the reading of Abū ʿAmr: {يَنصُرْكُمُ} [Āl ʿImrān: 160] and {يُشْعِرُكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 109] and the like. As for the third person, it follows the name of Allah the Exalted, and the first person is by iltifāt from third to first for magnification.

semin-durr:187-187.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَيَّانَ مُرْسَاهَا}: two views on it. One: that «أيان» is a fronted khabar and «مُرْساها» a postponed mubtadaʾ. The second: that «أيان» is accusative as an adverbial by an implied verb, which verb makes «مرساها» nominative as its agent; this is the position of Abū l-ʿAbbās. This clause is in the position of accusative because it is a badal al-ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) from «الساعة», and then it ought not to have been in the position of genitive, because it is a substitute for a genitive. Abū l-Baqāʾ stated it explicitly, saying: "The clause is in the position of genitive as a badal from «الساعة», its implied form being: 'they ask you about the time of the arrival of the Hour.'" Except that what prevents its being genitive in position is that the badal is in the intention of repeating the governor, and the governor is «يَسْألونك»; and asking is suspended by the interrogative, and it is transitive; he means the interrogative clause is then in the position of accusative after removal of the preposition, as if it were said: "they ask you, when is the anchoring of the Hour?" So in reality it is a badal from the position of «عن الساعة», because the position of the genitive noun is accusative; and its like among badals, in the best views on it: «عَرَفْتُ زيداً أبو مَنْ هو» ("I knew Zayd — whose father is he").
And «أيان» is an adverbial of time, indeclinable because it includes the meaning of the interrogative, and it is not declined; it is followed by the mubtadaʾ and the imperfect verb, not the past, unlike «متى», which is followed by both types. Most often «أيَّان» is interrogative, as in the poet's saying:
2352 - أيَّان تَقْضي حاجتي أيَّانا ... أما تَرى لفِعْلها إبَّانا
(When will you fulfil my need, when? Do you not see that there is a due time for doing it?)
It may also be conditional, jussive-governing two verbs. The poet said:
2353 - أيَّان نُؤْمِنْكَ تُؤْمَنْ غيرَنا وإذا ... لم تُدْرِكِ الأمنَ منَّا لم تزلْ حَذِرا
(Whenever we give you safety, you will be safe from others; and if you do not attain safety from us, you will remain wary.)
And another said:
2354 - إذا النَّعْجَةُ العَجْفاءُ باتت بقَفْرةٍ ... فأيَّان ما تَعْدِلْ بها الريحُ تَنْزِلِ
(When the lean ewe spends the night in a desolate place, wherever the wind turns her, she will alight.)
The eloquent form is fatḥa on its hamza, and this is the reading of the majority. Al-Sulamī read it with kasra, and it is the dialect of Sulaym. The grammarians differed about «أيَّان»: is it simple or compound? Some held that its origin is «أيّ أوانٍ», so the hamza was dropped against analogy and nothing was given in exchange for it, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ against analogy, so three yāʾs came together, which was found heavy, and one of them was dropped, and the word was built on fatḥa so it became ayyān. They also differed about it: is it derived or not? Abū l-Fatḥ held that it is derived from awaytu ilayhi ("I resorted to it"), because the part resorts to the whole, and the meaning is "what time and what act"; and its pattern is faʿlān or fiʿlān according to the two dialects, and he denied that its pattern is faʿʿāl derived from «أين», because «أين» is an adverbial of place and «أيان» an adverbial of time.
And «مُرْساها» may be an ism maṣdar and may be an ism zamān (noun of time). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«مُرْساها»: its anchoring or the time of its anchoring, that is, its establishment and fixing." The Shaykh said: "His supposing 'the time of its anchoring' is not good, because «أيَّان» is an inquiry about time, so it is not sound that it be a khabar about a time except figuratively, as the implied form would be 'at what time is the time of its anchoring,'" and it is good speech. It is said rasā yarsū: it stayed firm, and it is said only of a heavy thing, such as rasat al-safīna tarsū, and arsaytuhā.
His saying: {عِلْمُهَا}: a maṣdar annexed to its object, and the adverbial is its khabar. And His saying «في السماوات» admits of two views. One: that «في» has the meaning of «على», that is: "upon the inhabitants of the heavens," or it is heavy upon the very heavens and earth because of the splitting of this and the quaking of that. The second: that it is in its normal sense of containment, and the meaning is: its heaviness, which is its severity or the exaggeration in concealing it, occurred in these two containers.
His saying: {كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ}: this likening clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the object of «يسألونك». Regarding «عنها» there are two views. One: that it is attached to «يسألونك», and «كأنك حَفِيٌّ» is parenthetical, and its ṣila is omitted, its implied form being: "solicitous of it."
Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There is an advancing and delaying in the speech," and there is no need for that because all of these are connected to the verb, for His saying: /"كأنك حفيٌّ" is a ḥāl as passed. The second: that «عن» has the meaning of «الباء», just as «الباء» has the meaning of «عن», as in {فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً} [al-Furqān: 59] and {وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السمآء بالغمام} [al-Furqān: 25], because ḥafī is not transitive with «عن» but with «الباء», as in His saying {كَانَ بِي حَفِيّاً} [Maryam: 47], and it is made to include the meaning of something that is transitive with «عن», that is: "as though you were uncovering, through your solicitude, about it."
Al-ḥafī is the one who inquires thoroughly into a thing, who is assiduous about it, attentive to its affair. He said:
2355 - سؤال حفيٍّ عن أخيه كأنه ... بذُكْرَتِهِ وَسْنانُ أو مُتَواسِنُ
(The question of one solicitous about his brother, as though, by remembering him, he were drowsy or feigning drowsiness.)
And another said:
2356 - فلمَّا التقينا بَيَّن السيفُ بيننا ... لسائلةٍ عنا حَفِيٍّ سؤالُها
(When we met, the sword made clear between us, to a woman asking about us, whose asking is solicitous.)
And al-Aʿshā said:
2357 - فإنْ تَسْأَلي عني فيا رُبُّ سائلٍ ... حَفِيٍّ عن الأعشى به حيث أَصْعَدا
(If you ask about me — many a solicitous inquirer has asked about al-Aʿshā, wherever he went up-country.)
And al-iḥfāʾ is thorough inquiry, and from it "iḥfāʾ of the moustaches," and al-ḥāfī (barefoot), because his foot wore down in thorough travel. And al-ḥafāwa is kindness and gentleness.
ʿAbd Allāh read «حَفِيٌّ بها», and it is evidence for whoever claimed that «عَنْ» has the meaning of «الباء». And ḥafī is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, that is, maḥfūw (treated with solicitude). It was said: in the sense of fāʿil, that is: "as though you were exaggerating in asking about it and straining toward knowledge of its coming."

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنَا مَا وَعَدَنَا رَبُّنَا حَقًّا فَهَلْ وَجَدْتُمْ مَا وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ حَقًّا قَالُوا نَعَمْ فَأَذَّنَ مُؤَذِّنٌ بَيْنَهُمْ أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ) (٤٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ قَدْ وَجَدْنَا): «أَنْ» may be in the sense of أَيْ (explicative "that is"), and it may be the lightened form (mukhaffafa) [of أَنَّ].
(حَقًّا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it may be a second object, with وَجَدْنَا then in the sense of عَلِمْنَا ("we have known"). (مَا وَعَدَ رَبُّكُمْ): the object has been omitted from the second «وَعَدَ». So the implied form may be وَعَدَكُمْ ("He promised you"), and He omitted it because the first indicates it. The implied form may also be "what He promised the two parties", meaning our bliss and your punishment. And the implied form may be وَعَدَنَا ("He promised us"); what strengthens this is that what the people of the Fire are in is evil, and the verb used for that is أَوْعَدَ ("to threaten"), while وَعَدَ is used more often for good. (نَعَمْ): a particle with which a question is answered, affirming what was asked about. Its nūn and ʿayn are both with fatḥa; it is also read with kasra on the ʿayn, which is a dialect form; and it is permissible to put kasra on both of them by assimilation (itbāʿ). (بَيْنَهُمْ): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) of أَذَّنَ, and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of مُؤَذِّنٍ. (أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ): it is read with fatḥa on the hamza and the nūn without shadda; it is the lightened form, i.e. "that it is that Allah has cursed him". It may also be in the sense of أَيْ, because the proclamation (al-adhān) is a saying. It is also read with shadda on the nūn and the accusative of اللَّعْنَة, and that is plain. In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it was read with kasra on the hamza, i.e. "and he said: أَنْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ". [Translator's note: the kasra reading would be إِنَّ / إِنْ, though the printed text repeats «أَنْ».]

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَيَبْغُونَهَا عِوَجًا وَهُمْ بِالْآخِرَةِ كَافِرُونَ) (٤٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ): it may be genitive, accusative or nominative.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَبَيْنَهُمَا حِجَابٌ وَعَلَى الْأَعْرَافِ رِجَالٌ يَعْرِفُونَ كُلًّا بِسِيمَاهُمْ وَنَادَوْا أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ) (٤٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَادَوْا): the pronoun refers back to رِجَالٍ ("men"). (أَنْ سَلَامٌ): i.e. "that it is: peace"; and it may be in the sense of أَيْ (explicative "that is"). (لَمْ يَدْخُلُوهَا): i.e. the people of the Garden have not yet entered the Garden. (وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ): in entering it; i.e. they called out to them in this state, and on this view the words «وَهُمْ يَطْمَعُونَ» have no grammatical position. It is also said: the meaning is that they called out to them after they had entered, but they entered it while they had not been hoping for it; on this view the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا صُرِفَتْ أَبْصَارُهُمْ تِلْقَاءَ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ) (٤٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تِلْقَاءَ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun). Among the maṣdars there is no tifʿāl — with kasra on the tāʾ — except تِلْقَاءٌ and تِبْيَانٌ; that pattern comes only in nouns, such as التِّمْثَالُ, التِّمْسَاحُ and التِّقْصَارُ. The accusative of «تِلْقَاءَ» here is as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "in the direction of the people of the Fire".

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ الْأَعْرَافِ رِجَالًا يَعْرِفُونَهُمْ بِسِيمَاهُمْ قَالُوا مَا أَغْنَى عَنْكُمْ جَمْعُكُمْ وَمَا كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ) (٤٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَغْنَى): «مَا» may be negating, and it may be interrogative.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمْتُمْ لَا يَنَالُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلَا أَنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ) (٤٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَنَالُهُمُ): its implied form is "you swore concerning them that He would not reach them", so «لَا يَنَالُهُمُ» is the thing sworn to.
(ادْخُلُوا): its implied form is "so they turned to the people of the Garden and said: ادْخُلُوا (enter)". In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it is read وَادْخُلُوا [Translator's note: presumably the passive past "and they were made to enter", i.e. وَأُدْخِلُوا, as the following remark about "the declarative" indicates; the printed text gives «وَادْخُلُوا».] as a resumption, and that is said after they have entered. (لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ): if «ادْخُلُوا» is read as an imperative, the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "enter in safety"; and if it is read as a declarative (khabar), it is a turn from the third person to direct address.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَادَى أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ أَصْحَابَ الْجَنَّةِ أَنْ أَفِيضُوا عَلَيْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ أَوْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ حَرَّمَهُمَا عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ) (٥٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ أَفِيضُوا): «أَنْ» may be maṣdariyya (infinitival) or tafsīriyya (explicative). And (مِنَ الْمَاءِ): its implied form is "something of the water". (أَوْ مِمَّا): it is said that «أَوْ» is in the sense of the wāw ("and"), and His saying «حَرَّمَهُمَا» ("He has forbidden them both") was adduced as proof of that. It is also said: it is in its proper sense, and حَرَّمَهُمَا is according to the meaning, so there is an ellipsis in it, i.e. "each of them" or "both of them".

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ لَهْوًا وَلَعِبًا وَغَرَّتْهُمُ الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا فَالْيَوْمَ نَنْسَاهُمْ كَمَا نَسُوا لِقَاءَ يَوْمِهِمْ هَذَا وَمَا كَانُوا بِآيَاتِنَا يَجْحَدُونَ) (٥١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَهُمْ): it may be genitive, accusative or nominative. And (لَهْوًا): a second object, and the explanation is "a thing played with and a thing sported with". It may also be "they made their custom [a diversion]", because الدِّين has come in the sense of "custom" (al-ʿāda).

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ جِئْنَاهُمْ بِكِتَابٍ فَصَّلْنَاهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) (٥٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى عِلْمٍ): it may be that "We detailed it as containing knowledge", so that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ. It may also be a ḥāl from the agent, i.e. "We detailed it knowing", i.e. on the basis of knowledge from Us.
(هُدًى وَرَحْمَةً): two ḥāls, i.e. "possessing guidance and possessing mercy". It was also read in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَّا تَأْوِيلَهُ يَوْمَ يَأْتِي تَأْوِيلُهُ يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ قَدْ جَاءَتْ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِالْحَقِّ فَهَلْ لَنَا مِنْ شُفَعَاءَ فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنَا أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ قَدْ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ) (٥٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ يَأْتِي): it is an adverb (ẓarf) of «يَقُولُ». (فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنَا): it is accusative as the answer to the question. (أَوْ نُرَدُّ): the well-known reading is the nominative, and it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the position of «مِنْ شُفَعَاءَ», its implied form being "or will we be returned?". (فَنَعْمَلَ): also as the answer to the question. It is also read in the nominative, i.e. "so will we act?", and it then falls within the question. And the two of them are read in the accusative as the answer to the question.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثًا وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ بِأَمْرِهِ أَلَا لَهُ الْخَلْقُ وَالْأَمْرُ تَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ) (٥٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ): there are two views on its position. One of them: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «خَلَقَ», and on this view the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ is «اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ». The second: it is resumptive. يُغْشِي is without shadda and with ḍamma on the yāʾ; it is from أَغْشَى, and it takes two objects, i.e. "Allah covers the night over the day". It is also read «يُغَشِّي» with shadda, and the meaning is the same. It is also read «يَغْشِي» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and without shadda, with اللَّيْلُ as its fāʿil (agent). (يَطْلُبُهُ): a ḥāl from اللَّيْل or from النَّهَار. And (حَثِيثًا): a ḥāl from اللَّيْل, because it is the agent.
It may also be from النَّهَار, so that the implied form is "the night seeks the day, being urged on"; and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a swift seeking". (وَالشَّمْسَ): it is read in the accusative, the implied form being "and He created the sun"; and whoever read the nominative began a new sentence.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ) (٥٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَخُفْيَةً): it is read with ḍamma and with kasra on the khāʾ, and they are two dialect forms. The two maṣdars (verbal nouns) are ḥāls (circumstantials), and they may be a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Similar to it is (خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا).

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تُفْسِدُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ إِصْلَاحِهَا وَادْعُوهُ خَوْفًا وَطَمَعًا إِنَّ رَحْمَةَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) (٥٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَرِيبٌ): it was not made feminine only because He meant the rain. It is also said: الرَّحْمَة and التَّرَحُّم have one meaning. It is also said: it is by way of relation (al-nasab), i.e. "possessing nearness", as one says امْرَأَةٌ طَالِقٌ ("a divorced woman"). It is also said: it is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, as they said لِحْيَةٌ دَهِينٌ ("an oiled beard") and كَفٌّ خَضِيبٌ ("a dyed palm"). It is also said: they meant the place, i.e. the place of Allah's mercy is near. It is also said: by dropping [the feminine marker] He distinguished between قَرِيب in the sense of kinship and قَرِيب in other senses.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُرْسِلُ الرِّيَاحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ حَتَّى إِذَا أَقَلَّتْ سَحَابًا ثِقَالًا سُقْنَاهُ لِبَلَدٍ مَيِّتٍ فَأَنْزَلْنَا بِهِ الْمَاءَ فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ كَذَلِكَ نُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتَى لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) (٥٧).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بُشْرًا): it is read with nūn and with the shīn, both with ḍamma [i.e. نُشُرًا], and it is a plural. On its singular there are two views. One of them: نَشُورٌ, like صَبُورٌ and صُبُرٌ; on this view faʿūl may be in the sense of fāʿil, i.e. "reviving the earth", and it may be in the sense of mafʿūl, like رَكُوبٌ in the sense of مَرْكُوبٌ ("ridden"), i.e. "spread out" after folding, or "revived", i.e. "brought to life", from your saying أَنْشَرَ اللَّهُ الْمَيِّتَ فَهُوَ مُنْشَرٌ ("Allah revived the dead, so he is revived"). [The second:] it may be the plural of نَاشِرٌ, like نَازِلٌ and نُزُلٌ. It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn, by lightening the ḍamma-vowelled form. It is also read نَشْرًا with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the shīn; it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نَشَرَ ("he spread") after folding, or from your saying أَنْشَرَ اللَّهُ الْمَيِّتَ فَنُشِرَ, i.e. "he lived"; and its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "spreading" or "possessing spreading", as you say جَاءَ رَكْضًا, i.e. رَاكِضًا ("he came running"). It is also read «بُشُرًا» with bāʾ and two ḍammas; it is the plural of بَشِيرٌ ("bearer of good news"), like قَلِيبٌ and قُلُبٌ. It is also read the same way except with sukūn on the shīn, for lightness; and similar to it in meaning is (يُرْسِلَ الرِّيَاحَ مُبَشِّرَاتٍ). It is also read «بُشْرَى», like حُبْلَى, i.e. "possessing good tidings". It is also read «بَشْرًا» with fatḥa on the bāʾ and sukūn on the shīn; it is the maṣdar of بَشَرْتُهُ, when you gave him good news. [Translator's note: the heading word printed as (بُشْرًا) does not match the first reading described, which is نُشُرًا with nūn.] (سَحَابًا): the plural of سَحَابَةٌ ("cloud"); and that is why He described it with the plural [ثِقَالًا]. (لِبَلَدٍ): i.e. "to revive a land". (بِهِ الْمَاءَ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the bāʾ [Translator's note: so in the printed text; presumably «الْبَلَد», "the land", is meant.], or the pronoun of the clouds, or the pronoun of the wind; and likewise the hāʾ in the second «بِهِ».

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْبَلَدُ الطَّيِّبُ يَخْرُجُ نَبَاتُهُ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ وَالَّذِي خَبُثَ لَا يَخْرُجُ إِلَّا نَكِدًا كَذَلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ الْآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَشْكُرُونَ) (٥٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَخْرُجُ نَبَاتُهُ): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ, ḍamma on the rāʾ and the nominative of النَّبَات. It is also read the same way but with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as a passive (ʿalā mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu). And it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ, kasra on the rāʾ and the accusative of النَّبَات, i.e. "so Allah brings out", or "the water". (بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِ) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَخْرُجُ. (إِلَّا نَكِدًا): with fatḥa on the nūn and kasra on the kāf; it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also read with fatḥa on both, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "possessing hardship". It is also read with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the kāf, and that too is a maṣdar; it is a dialect form. And «يُخْرِجُ» is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ, with نَكِدًا as its object.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ فَقَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) (٥٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ): «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), «إِلَهٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَكُمْ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also said: the khabar is omitted, i.e. "you have no god in existence", and «لَكُمْ» is specification and clarification. As for «غَيْرُهُ» in the nominative, there are two views on it. One of them: it is a naʿt (adjective) of «إِلَهٍ» according to its position. The second: it is a badal (substitute) from the position, like لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ. It is also read in the accusative as an exception, and in the genitive as an adjective according to the wording. (عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ): the day is described as great, and what is meant is the greatness of what is in it.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ إِنَّا لَنَرَاكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ) (٦٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ قَوْمِهِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمَلَأ. And (نَرَاكَ): from seeing with the eye, so that (فِي ضَلَالٍ) is a ḥāl. It may also be from seeing with the heart (i.e. knowing), so that it is a second object.

ukberi-tibyan:61-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ لَيْسَ بِي ضَلَالَةٌ وَلَكِنِّي رَسُولٌ مِنْ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٦١) أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنْصَحُ لَكُمْ وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ) (٦٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ): it may be resumptive, and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of رَسُولٌ according to the meaning, because the messenger is the pronoun in «لَكِنِّي»; and had it been يُبَلِّغُكُمْ ("he conveys to you") it would have been permissible, because it would then refer back to the wording رَسُولٌ. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the governing element in it being the preposition in His saying (مِنْ رَبِّ). (وَأَعْلَمُ مِنَ اللَّهِ): in the sense of أَعْرِفُ ("I know"), so it takes one object, which is «مَا»; it is in the sense of الَّذِي, or an indefinite noun described [by what follows]. On مِنَ اللَّهِ there are two views. One of them: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَعْلَمُ, i.e. the beginning of my knowledge is from Allah. The second: it is a ḥāl from «مَا» or from the omitted resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid).

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ وَلِتَتَّقُوا وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) (٦٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of (ذِكْرٌ), and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to جَاءَكُمْ.
(عَلَى رَجُلٍ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذِكْرٌ, i.e. "sent down upon a man", and it may be attached to جَاءَكُمْ according to the meaning, because it carries the meaning of "sent down to you". In the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "upon the heart of a man" or "the tongue of a man".

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ وَأَغْرَقْنَا الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمًا عَمِينَ) (٦٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْفُلْكِ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِينَ» or from the nominative pronoun in مَعَهُ. The origin of (عَمِينَ) is عَمِيِينَ; the first [yāʾ] was given sukūn and dropped.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِلَى عَادٍ أَخَاهُمْ هُودًا قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ إِلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ أَفَلَا تَتَّقُونَ) (٦٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُودًا): a badal (substitute) from أَخَاهُمْ, and أَخَاهُمْ is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We sent to ʿĀd"; and likewise the beginnings of the stories that come after it.

ukberi-tibyan:193-193.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنْ تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدَى لَا يَتَّبِعُوكُمْ سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ) (١٩٣).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ): this has been discussed under His saying: (سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ).
And (أَمْ أَنْتُمْ صَامِتُونَ): a nominal clause in the position of a verbal clause; the implied wording is: أَدَعَوْتُمُوهُمْ أَمْ صَمَتُّمْ ("whether you called them or kept silent").

ukberi-tibyan:194-194.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ عِبَادٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ فَادْعُوهُمْ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ) (١٩٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ): the majority read it with the nūn doubled (tashdīd); and (عِبَادٌ) is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ. And (أَمْثَالُكُمْ) is a naʿt (adjective) to it, and the returning pronoun (al-ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. تَدْعُو بِهِمْ. It is also read «عِبَادًا», and it is then a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted returning pronoun, with أَمْثَالُكُمُ as the khabar. And «إِنْ» is read without doubling, in which case it has the meaning of «مَا» ("not"), and عِبَادًا is its khabar, and «أَمْثَالَكُمْ» is read in the accusative as a naʿt to عِبَادًا. It has also been read «أَمْثَالُكُمْ» in the nominative, on the basis that عِبَادًا is a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun and «أَمْثَالُكُمْ» is the khabar. And إِنْ in the meaning of «مَا» does not govern according to Sībawayh, and does govern according to al-Mubarrad.

ukberi-tibyan:195-195.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِهَا أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ يَبْطِشُونَ بِهَا أَمْ لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا أَمْ لَهُمْ آذَانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا قُلِ ادْعُوا شُرَكَاءَكُمْ ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنْظِرُونِ) (١٩٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلِ ادْعُوا): it is read with ḍamma on the lām and with kasra; we have mentioned this under His saying: (فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ).

ukberi-tibyan:196-196.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى الصَّالِحِينَ) (١٩٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ): the majority read it with the first yāʾ doubled and the second with fatḥa, and this is the original form. It is also read with the second [yāʾ] dropped in pronunciation, because it is vowelless and what follows it is vowelless; and it is read with fatḥa on the first yāʾ and no yāʾ after it, the second being dropped from pronunciation for lightness.

ukberi-tibyan:201-201.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا إِذَا مَسَّهُمْ طَائِفٌ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ تَذَكَّرُوا فَإِذَا هُمْ مُبْصِرُونَ) (٢٠١).
His saying, Exalted is He: (طَيْفٌ): it is read with the yāʾ undoubled, and there are two views about it. The first: its origin is طَيِّفٌ, like مَيِّتٍ, and it was lightened. The second: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of طَافَ يَطِيفُ, said when something encompasses a thing. It is also said: it is the maṣdar of يَطُوفُ, the wāw being changed into yāʾ although it is vowelless, just as it was changed in أَيْدٍ; but this is far-fetched. And it is read طَائِفٌ, on the pattern fāʿil.

ukberi-tibyan:202-202.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِخْوَانُهُمْ يَمُدُّونَهُمْ فِي الْغَيِّ ثُمَّ لَا يُقْصِرُونَ) (٢٠٢).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَمُدُّونَهُمْ): with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the mīm, from مَدَّ يَمُدُّ, like His saying: (وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِي طُغْيَانِهِمْ); and it is read with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the mīm, from أَمَدَّهُ إِمْدَادًا. (فِي الْغَيِّ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb mentioned, and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun or from the agent pronoun.

ukberi-tibyan:204-204.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَأَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ) (٢٠٤).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ): the lām may be in the meaning of "for Allah" (لِلَّهِ), i.e. "for its sake" (لِأَجْلِهِ); it may be redundant (zāʾida), i.e. فَاسْتَمِعُوهُ ("so listen to it"); and it may be in the meaning of إِلَى ("to").

ukberi-tibyan:205-205.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ فِي نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ بِالْغُدُوِّ وَالْآصَالِ وَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ) (٢٠٥).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also said: it is a maṣdar of a verb not from the [root] mentioned but from its meaning. (وَدُونَ الْجَهْرِ): conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تَضَرُّع, and the implied sense is: "moderate" (مُقْتَصِدِينَ). (بِالْغُدُوِّ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to اذْكُرْ. (وَالْآصَالِ): a plural of a plural, because the singular is أَصِيلٌ, and faʿīl is not pluralised on afʿāl but on fuʿul, and then fuʿul is pluralised on afʿāl; the origin is أَصِيلٌ and أَصْلٌ «[Translator's note: so vocalised in the text; the fuʿul form just described would be أُصُلٌ]», then آصَالٌ.
It is read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, وَالْإِيصَالِ, with kasra on the hamza and a yāʾ after it; this is the maṣdar of آصَلْنَا, said when we enter the time of al-aṣīl (late afternoon).
My Lord, make it easy (رب يسر).

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي وَأَنَا لَكُمْ نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ) (٦٨).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَاصِحٌ أَمِينٌ): it [أَمِينٌ] is faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle).

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَعَجِبْتُمْ أَنْ جَاءَكُمْ ذِكْرٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ عَلَى رَجُلٍ مِنْكُمْ لِيُنْذِرَكُمْ وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ جَعَلَكُمْ خُلَفَاءَ مِنْ بَعْدِ قَوْمِ نُوحٍ وَزَادَكُمْ فِي الْخَلْقِ بَسْطَةً فَاذْكُرُوا آلَاءَ اللَّهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) (٦٩).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِي الْخَلْقِ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «بَسْطَةً», and it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to زَادَكُمْ. الْآلَاءُ ("the favours") is a plural, and on its singular there are three dialect forms: إِلًى — with kasra on the hamza and a single alif after the lām; the same with fatḥa on the hamza [أَلًى]; and with kasra on the hamza, sukūn on the lām and a yāʾ after it [إِلْيٌ].

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا لِنَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ وَحْدَهُ وَنَذَرَ مَا كَانَ يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُنَا فَأْتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ) (٧٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَحْدَهُ): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with its augment letters dropped. On its position there are two views. One of them: it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اللَّه, i.e. "that we should worship Allah as singled out and declared one"; and some of them said: it is a ḥāl from the agents, i.e. "declaring His oneness". The second: it is an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "that we should worship Allah [alone] as He is"; Yūnus said this.
